## complete derivation or exact first unsupported line

### Convexity for fixed actual-run laws

Write t_l=ln lambda_l and A_{jl}=1_{j in R_l}. Expansion gives

    D(e^t)=sum_{empty != R subset [N]} exp(sum_{l in R}(t_l+ln pi_l)).

Thus F(t)=v ln D(e^t)-c dot t is convex, being a log-sum-exp minus a linear function. Each g_j(t)=sum_l A_{jl}exp(t_l)-1 is convex. This statement does not require a convex objective in lambda coordinates. Strict feasibility holds by taking all lambda small and positive. Duplicate supports give distinct columns/draw labels and remain subject to the same coordinate rows; they must not be silently combined in a cost calculation. Every nonconstant gate has nonempty relevant support. Constant-false gates are removed; a constant-true gate makes f constant and H=I=0. Uncovered coordinates have the empty incidence sum zero. If a retained gate has c_l>0, its weight cannot be set to zero with finite fixed-posterior cost except in a simultaneous common-scaling limit where the normalizer cancels; see the boundary discussion below.

Here is a dual lower certificate without a solver. Choose a probability law nu on nonempty root sets, with marginals r_l=Pr_nu(l in R), and coordinate prices y_j>=0. Define q_l=sum_j A_{jl}y_j and b_l=c_l-v r_l. Require b_l>=0, and q_l>0 when b_l>0. With H_nat(nu)=-sum nu ln nu, define

    L(nu,y)=v[H_nat(nu)+sum_l r_l ln pi_l]-sum_j y_j
             +sum_{l:b_l>0} b_l[1+ln(q_l/b_l)].

Then inf_feasible F >= L. To prove this, the elementary finite Gibbs identity gives ln D(e^t)>=H_nat(nu)+sum_l r_l(t_l+ln pi_l). Add sum_j y_j g_j(t), which is <=0 on feasible points. Its infimum over unconstrained t separates into inf_t[-b_l t+q_l exp(t)]. For b_l,q_l>0 the value is b_l[1+ln(q_l/b_l)], attained at exp(t)=b_l/q_l. If b_l=0 the infimum is zero (also when q_l=0). If b_l<0 or b_l>0=q_l it is -infinity, hence those choices give no useful certificate. This proves weak duality directly; no unjustified interchange of supremum and infimum is used.

For a feasible positive lambda, take nu_*(R)=product_{l in R}(pi_l lambda_l)/D(lambda). Its marginals are rational for rational lambda and pi:

    r_l=pi_l lambda_l product_{k!=l}(1+pi_k lambda_k)/D.

If nonnegative rational prices satisfy

    c_l-v r_l=lambda_l q_l,
    y_j(sum_l A_{jl}lambda_l-1)=0,

the displayed dual bound equals F(ln lambda) exactly. Gibbs equality, scalar minimizer equality (including b_l=q_l=0), and complementary slackness prove the equality and global optimality. Equivalently the gradient of the convex Lagrangian vanishes, which also proves sufficiency directly. This is the claimed verifiable duality assertion: any such certificate is exact. Only the proved sufficient certificate and weak duality are asserted and used here. No necessity theorem, minimax interchange, or assertion that every instance has a finite optimizer is needed.

In particular the actual family member (r,m)=(1,2) with the fixed posterior below has v=15/16, c_l=17/32, pi_l=1/4, lambda_l=1/2, r_l=9/17. The common coordinate price y=19/272 and private prices zero give

    (15/16)(9/17)-17/32+(1/2)(19/272)=0.

This certifies a global optimum for that actual fixed-posterior instance. Three other heterogeneous examples in WEIGHT_CERTIFICATE.json certify abstract program inputs only; their c values are not asserted to be Boolean-realizable run marginals.

For the symmetric r,m family below c_l=c_total/m. Permuting t preserves feasibility and F; convex averaging therefore shows the infimum can be taken at equal weights, even if it is not attained. Set lambda_l=z/m, 0<z<=1. The scalar derivative with respect to ln z is v E_nu K-c_total, where K is root count. For m>=2 its derivative again is v Var_nu K>0, since both singleton and double root sets have positive mass. Hence there is at most one stationary scale; otherwise the upper boundary is optimal. For m>=2 our laws have c_total>v, so the objective tends to +infinity as z decreases to zero and a finite equal-weight minimizer exists. For m=1, c_total=v and the scale-dependent expression is constant. For general fixed laws, c_total=v can instead produce an unattained boundary infimum: if every output uses exactly one among several eligible gates, scaling all weights down cancels the leading ln scale. Consequently zero weights/boundary limits cannot simply be excluded when claiming the variational infimum.

### Joint posterior/weight optimization is not convex

Take the actual Boolean function f=x_1 represented by two identical dictator gates. There are two actual partition runs for its singleton spectral set, one rooted at each gate, and pi_1=pi_2=1/2. After optimizing the posterior, S_B=(lambda_1+lambda_2)/2 and the natural-unit residual is

    ln[D/S_B]=ln[1+lambda_1 lambda_2/(2(lambda_1+lambda_2))].

Put lambda_1=exp(t+s), lambda_2=exp(t-s). This becomes ln[1+exp(t)/(4 cosh s)]. At t=ln(1/4), s=0 the incidence inequality has strict slack and the second derivative in s is -1/17. Thus the full posterior-optimized objective is not convex in log weights, even for an actual Boolean example. The fixed-law convex program and its dual must not be transferred to that broader objective.

### Full shared-core residual certificate

Put p=2^-r, q=2^-m, b=1-q, gamma=6/5. For core U and private T, every nonempty set has coefficient 2p Bhat(T). Bhat(empty)=b; every nonempty private T has |Bhat(T)|=q. Therefore

    P(U union T)=4p^2 b^2 if T empty and U nonempty,
    P(U union T)=4p^2 q^2 if T nonempty (including U empty),
    v=4pb(1-pb), I_core=2rp b, I_data=2pmq.

These also follow directly from physical pivotal probabilities. Choose the following laws, fixed independently of lambda:

* If U nonempty and T empty: one gate owns U; average uniformly over all m root gates, giving H(eta)=log m.
* If U nonempty and T nonempty, t=|T|: select one of the t private gates as root, assign all U to it along with its private coordinate, and attach the other t-1 private gates through the first selected core coordinate. Average uniformly over the t root choices and (t-1)! ordered child-label sequences. There are exactly t! distinct actual queue runs, so H(eta)=log(t!).
* If U empty: each of the t private coordinates is assigned to its own gate; all t gates are roots. The source components are singleton gates, and the root queue's fixed order gives one actual run, with entropy zero.

Every run visits each used gate once, uses disjoint assigned subsets, and terminates. The root reaches every other used gate when U is nonempty, so the star is a permitted spanning forest with one source component. Ordered child draws are distinct actual random outcomes, not permutations of an abstract written edge list. The selected common attachment has positive probability under the uniform multiset draw. Every prescribed label draw is positive with lambda=1/m.

Let E denote spectral-weighted expectation on nonempty sets and these laws, K the root count, and V the used-gate count. Direct tensor summation gives

    E K-v=4p^2 q(m/2-b),
    E |T|=I_data,
    E V-v=2p q[m-2(1-q)]>0 for m>=2.

For the last identity, E V=core-only mass + E|T|, and core-only mass=4p(1-p)b^2. The difference is zero for m=1 and any r; it is positive for m>=2 because m>=2>2b.

The root rarity is r+1, and D=(1+p/(2m))^m-1. Expansion and exp(a)-1<=a exp(a), a=p/2, give

    log D=-(r+1)+delta, 0<=delta<=(p/2)log e.

Hence normalization plus rarity is exactly v delta+(r+1)(E K-v). Since K-1<=|T| on the empty-core exceptional sets,

    E K-v<=p I_data,
    (r+1)(E K-v)<=I_data,
    v delta <=(log e) I_core.

Here (r+1)2^-r<=1 and v<=4pb. Both Lambda and log Z were retained through log D; neither is silently dropped.

Write G(U)=gamma sum_{j selected in U} log(j/position_U(j)), using ranks j=1..r. Every selected core coordinate contributes this same term, regardless of root. Conditional on selection of rank j, its predecessor count is Bin(j-1,1/2). Direct binomial summation gives E[1/(1+Bin)]=2(1-2^-j)/j. Jensen for the concave log therefore gives expected log(j/(1+Bin))<=1, so the uniform-U average of G is <=gamma r/2. Also sum_T Bhat(T)^2=b (B is an indicator). Consequently

    E G(U)<=4p^2 b 2^r gamma r/2=gamma I_core.

For a private leaf the subset congestion gamma log(|U|+1) cancels its negative private rank term, leaving exactly gamma log(r+1). For the inside root the private rank cost is gamma log((r+1)/(|U|+1)) and congestion is zero. Empty-core roots also cost gamma log(r+1). Thus all private rank/congestion terms together are <=gamma log(r+1) I_data<=gamma I_core: use log(r+1)<=r, m 2^-m<=1/2 and b>=1/2.

Core-only labels cancel against log m actual-root entropy. On every other set, the remaining label cost minus posterior entropy is at most |T| log m; the -log(t!) saving stays nonpositive. Therefore it is <=I_data log m=2p m q log m<=4p<=4 I_core. For the middle bound log m<=m and m^2/2^m<=2 suffice: verify m=1,2,3 and use the ratio ((m+1)/m)^2/2<1 for m>=3. I_core>=rp>=p.

The complete residual, including all subset congestion, M=1 order costs, ranks, root labels, rarity and actual-run entropy, thus obeys

    R <= (4+2gamma+log e) I_core+I_data < 8 I(f).

The strict numerical comparison requires no floating point: ln 2>5/8 follows already from the first term 2/3 of its positive atanh series; hence log e<8/5 and 4+12/5+log e<8. For m=1 the same bound is valid without any multiple-root or label charge.

For a paid scale prior choose lambda_l^(j)=2^-j/m and w_j=1/[(j+1)(j+2)] for j>=0. These weights telescope to one; each whole conditioned generator is a subprobability. Selecting j=0 pays exactly v bits because w_0=1/2, and v<=2I_core/r<=2I. The complete residual plus this explicit prior is <=10I. This is an upper certificate at a feasible global vector, not a claim that uniform weights are optimal in every r,m case.

### New lead direction: geometric sunflower weights and the affine-plane obstruction

The B02 notes appeared at 2026-10-11 22:45 UTC, after this stage began, and were read in full before final persistence. They identify PI-J (prime-implicant whole-set coding) as the stream target and direct A009 to the outer fractional expression eq:outerfractional. The following is a source-bound test of that existing mechanism, not a new broad candidate. A008's finished dictionary report was also read: its sunflower quotient uses a different generator, so its bound neither replaces nor contradicts this residual.

For the r=1 sunflower, assign a common-coordinate pivotal input to the first positive private literal. Then alpha_0=b=1-2^-m, q_{0,l}=2^-l/b for l=1..m; a private-coordinate derivative has alpha_l=2^-m and only gate l eligible, so q_{l,l}=1. Choose the global rational weights lambda_l=2^-l. The common incidence sum is 1-2^-m<1, and each private row is 2^-l<=1. Put a=11/48. The outer sum satisfies

    S_0=b^(-1/2) sum_{l=1}^m 2^(-13l/48)
        <=sqrt(2)/(2^(13/48)-1)<9,
    log S_l=(11/48)l.

The last strict bound is elementary: 13/48>1/4, (7/6)^4<2, and sqrt(2)<3/2. Thus the pressure P=(48/5)sum_j alpha_j log S_j is at most (192/5)b+(11/5)2^-m m(m+1)/2 <41 I, using m(m+1)2^-m<=3/2 and I>=1. The latter bound follows from m=1,2,3 and the recurrence ratio (m+2)/(2m)<=1 for m>=2. This removes the uniform-weight (11/48)log m contribution inside every log S_j. The source's C_0<41 and v log Z<=0 yield a coarse H<82I, already known for this Boolean class; the new directional fact is the bounded fractional pressure with one explicit global vector and a specified tie rule. No entropy H is an input to the weights.

For each prime power Q>=16, let the coordinates be the Q^2 points of the affine plane over F_Q. Define f_Q=1 iff some affine line has all its Q point bits positive; otherwise f_Q=-1. There are N=Q(Q+1) genuine conjunction gates and k=Q+1 gates incident to each point. All are prime implicants: if a positive pattern contains a line, its minimal positive subset is that entire line; a set of fewer than Q points cannot contain any line. Conversely every line is minimal positive. All gate supports are nonempty and distinct, each cover has M_l=1, and each pi_l=2^-Q.

Fix a point j and a line l through it. Conditional on all Q-1 other points of l being positive, an alternative incident line is ready with probability 2^(-(Q-1)), since its other points are disjoint from l. A nonincident line has at most one forced positive point, so its probability of being fully positive at the j-negative endpoint is at most the same quantity. A union bound over N-1 other lines gives probability at least 1-epsilon_Q that no such alternative occurs, where

    epsilon_Q=Q(Q+1)2^(-(Q-1))<1/2 for every integer Q>=16.

These clean events for different lines through j are disjoint and make j pivotal. Therefore

    alpha_j >= k 2^(-(Q-1))(1-epsilon_Q)>0.

For ANY fixed disjoint pointwise tie decomposition of this derivative among pivotal line gates, each piece's squared norm is at most 2^(-(Q-1)). Hence its normalized mass obeys q_{j,l}<=1/[k(1-epsilon_Q)]<=2/k. These are precisely the disjoint signed pieces with masses summing to one required by the source outerfractional formula.

Every feasible global lambda has sum_{l incident j}lambda_l<=1. With a=11/48 and beta=1/[2(1+a)]=24/59, Holder gives the local relaxation bound

    S_j=sum_l sqrt(q_{j,l})lambda_l^-a
        >=(sum_l q_{j,l}^beta)^(1+a)
        >=(k/2)^(35/48).

The first inequality follows by applying Holder to q_l^beta=(sqrt(q_l)lambda_l^-a)^(1/(1+a)) lambda_l^(a/(1+a)). The second uses sum q=1 and q_l<=2/k, so sum q_l^beta>= (2/k)^(beta-1). This uses only the coordinate row, and thus holds for ALL simultaneous global incidence vectors; zeros with positive piece mass give infinite S_j rather than evade the bound. Consequently

    (48/5)sum_j alpha_j log S_j >= 7 I(f_Q) log((Q+1)/2).

Uniform lambda_l=1/k is feasible. Since sum sqrt(q_{j,l})<=sqrt k, it also gives pressure <=7I log k. Thus the optimized positive pressure grows logarithmically, between these two explicit bounds. No global weight choice repairs it. In addition v log Z cannot cancel that divergence: D=product_l(1+pi_l lambda_l)-1, log Z alone may diverge if weights shrink, but the positive pressure then rises; for the statement here only the nonnegative pressure requested by the lead is being bounded below. No claim about the infimum of the FULL expression with v log Z is inferred from this pressure lower bound. Its exact remaining cancellation is an additional question if one attempts to use this outer theorem rather than the whole-set forest mechanism.

This resolves the lead's requested O(I) pressure test negatively for the affine-plane DNF. The obstruction is the almost uniform distribution of genuinely pivotal line witnesses at each point, producing at least (35/48)log((Q+1)/2) in log S_j even after a local fractional relaxation. It does not disprove FEI, PI-J, or the posterior forest cost bound: all retain whole-set label sharing absent from this coordinatewise coarsening. Analytic finite-geometry incidence and a union bound establish the all-Q obstruction; no exponentially large truth-table computation is claimed.

## complete derivation or exact first unsupported line

### 1. Consume and independently reconstruct the retained-normalizer diagnostic

Write rho=2^-q, k=q+1, u=sum_l lambda_l, z_j=sum_{l through j}lambda_l, and P=(48/5)sum_j alpha_j log S_j. The stage-1 clean-pivotal-event bound gives normalized pivotal-piece mass <=2/k for every tie rule and all q>=16. Holder retaining the row mass gives

    P >=7I log(k/2)-(11/5)sum_j alpha_j log z_j.

Affine translation symmetry makes alpha_j constant. Double-counting incidences gives average_j z_j=u/q, hence Jensen implies

    P >=7I log(k/2)+(11/5)I log(q/u), 0<u<=q.

Let D=product(1+rho lambda_l)-1 and Z=D/(1+D). Expansion D>=rho u and monotonicity of x/(1+x) give

    log Z >=-q+log u-log(1+rho q).

The physical influence lower bound I>=2qN rho(1-epsilon), epsilon=2N rho<1/2, and the true-event union bound v<=4N rho give qv<=4I and v<=I. In particular v-(11/5)I<0. After adding the preceding inequalities, the scale-dependent coefficient of log u is negative, so its minimum is at u=q. Therefore

    P+v log Z >=7I log(k/2)+v log q-qv-v log(1+rho q)
               >=[7log(k/2)-5]I.

This proves A007's retained-normalizer clause independently, with no repair, at the exact stated scope. It rules out a coordinatewise rescue, including arbitrarily small scales; it does not address the actual whole-set forest label count. That is the first missing term connecting the previous lower bound to PI-J. We now pay that term for the affine-plane family.

### 2. A fixed actual-forest rule

Fix all line orders globally. If a nonempty spectral set A is contained in a line, choose the first such line and assign ALL of A to it. The run has one used gate, one root, no children, and s=kappa=|A|, so subset congestion is zero. For |A|>=2 the containing line is unique. For singletons any fixed first-line rule is sufficient.

Otherwise assign every point j in A to its first incident line. Discard empty owners, form the directed incidence graph l->l' when A_l intersects R_l', choose the least gate in every source strongly connected component, and grow a deterministic directed spanning forest from these roots. Choose the first allowed attachment point on every edge and a deterministic child draw order. A source-SCC root reaches every gate in its component, and every component is reached from some source in the finite condensation DAG; so this produces a finite forest visiting every used gate once. Its selected subsets partition A. Positive lambda and the incidence rows guarantee positive prescribed child-label probabilities. The uniform multiset and subset choices in the source generator also give positive probability. Thus this is an actual terminating queue run, not an abstract cover counted as a successful run.

The prime-implicant table is exact: every positive input contains a line, and a minimal positive support must be exactly that line. Uniform width and distinct lines exclude proper containment between line gates. There are no constant, empty-support, or duplicate gates. For the chosen point-mass law H(eta_A)=0; any improvement by averaging actual runs is optional, not required.

### 3. Ideal union amplitudes and a paid spectral error

Let b_l be the positive line indicator, K(x)=sum_l b_l(x), f=2*1[K>=1]-1, and G=2K-1. G is a real approximation, not a Boolean function; we do not apply FEI or any entropy inequality to G. Put e=f-G. Pointwise,

    e(x)^2=4(K-1)_+^2 <=4K(K-1).

Distinct affine lines meet in at most one point. Therefore E(b_l b_l')<=2^(1-2q) for l!=l', giving the exact Parseval error bound

    E2:=||e||_2^2 <=8N(N-1)4^-q <=8N^2 4^-q.

For nonempty A, |Ghat(A)|=2rho times the number of lines containing A. Its sign is the common conjunction-character sign; the binary checker uses (-1)^|A|. Hence Ghat vanishes on all off-line sets. On sets of size >=2 contained in a line there is exactly one ideal amplitude. The only coherent overlap is at singletons, where its multiplicity is k. No incoherent spectral law is substituted for the actual f law.

On good sets contained in a line, write gamma=6/5 and

    F_l(A)=gamma sum_{j in A} log[r_l(j)/(|A intersect predecessors_l(j)|+1)].

Let D=(1+rho/k)^N-1, a=N rho/k=q rho. Expansion and exp(a)-1<=a exp(a) give

    q+log D+log k = log N+delta =: c,
    0<=delta<=a log e.

Here the root rarity q and the negative normalization have been retained together; c>=0. Every good set's EXACT conditioned residual cost is C_A=c+F_l(A). For q>=16, D<1, since D<=a exp(a)<2a<1, with a<=1/4096. The conditioning term is negative but has already paid the good-set root rarity before it is bounded.

For one conjunction with a fixed order, a uniformly chosen subset selects each rank with probability 1/2. Conditional on selection of rank j, its predecessor count is Bin(j-1,1/2), and E[1/(1+Bin)]=2(1-2^-j)/j. Jensen gives conditional log rank at most one, hence the uniform-subset mean of F_l is <=gamma q/2. This elementary binomial estimate was used in stage 1; we reuse it, rather than claiming a new rank lemma.

It follows by summing the ideal amplitudes over each line, and separately upper-bounding coherent singleton amplitudes, that

    sum_good Ghat(A)^2 <=4N rho+4q^2 k^2 rho^2,
    sum_good Ghat(A)^2 F_selected(A)
        <=2gamma Nq rho+4gamma q^2 k^2 log q rho^2.

For the second inequality, sets of size >=2 have a unique line; the sum over all single-line subsets already controls their rank bill. Add the entire singleton ideal mass, at rank cost at most gamma log q. This deliberately double-counts some singleton rank mass as an upper bound, avoiding any silent cancellation of shared amplitudes.

### 4. Transfer the full cost to the actual Boolean spectrum

For every good frequency, fhat^2<=(2Ghat^2+2ehat^2). All good costs C_A are nonnegative. If C_max bounds their maximum, summation gives

    good residual <=2 sum_good Ghat(A)^2 C_A+2 C_max E2.

For bad/off-line A, Ghat(A)=0 so fhat(A)^2=ehat(A)^2, and their entire mass is <=E2. A generic actual forest has at most |A| used gates/roots, kappa_l<=q, and ranks <=q. Thus

    B_lambda(A) <= |A|[q+log k+2gamma log q]
                 <=q^2[q+log k+2gamma log q]=:B_max.

This pays gate labels, root rarity, subset congestion and ranks together, not just a rank-tail statistic. Its cover multiplicity term is zero because M=1. Since log D<0, each bad set's complete cost log D+B is at most B, so

    bad residual <=B_max E2.

The spectral error is used once in the two good/bad subcollections; their upper bounds may conservatively each use the full E2, as displayed. No credit is claimed twice as an exact identity.

For integer q>=16, log q<=q/4. Indeed equality holds at 16, and 2^(1/4)>7/6>17/16>=(q+1)/q makes 2^(q/4)>=q propagate to successive integers. Also log k<=1+log q<=5q/16 and log N<=1+2log q<=9q/16. The positive atanh series gives log e<8/5, so delta<=q/16. Therefore

    c<=5q/8,
    C_max <=c+gamma q log q <=q^2/2,
    B_max <=(153/80)q^3 <2q^3.

Combining these bounds and the ideal expectations gives the complete source residual upper bound

    R <= (49/5)Nq rho+(37/5)q^3 k^2 rho^2
         +8N^2(q^2+2q^3)rho^2.                         (U)

In particular the used-gate label bill is small because one gate owns the typical entire spectral set; the common read k is not charged separately to each point. The rare off-line mass pays every worst-case root/label/rank charge through its explicit E2 bound.

### 5. Analytic all-parameter certificate

Fix a point j and one incident line. Conditional on its q-1 other points being positive, every other incident line is ready with probability rho*2. Every nonincident line is fully positive at the j-negative endpoint with probability at most 2rho, since it contains at most one forced point. The union bound excludes all alternative lines with failure at most epsilon=2N rho. Clean events for the k incident lines are disjoint, so

    alpha_j >=2k rho(1-epsilon),
    I(f_q)>=2Nq rho(1-epsilon)>0.

This is a physical influence calculation, not an entropy or surrogate lower bound. Divide (U) by that lower bound to obtain

    R/I <= [49/5+(37/5)N rho+8N(q+2q^2)rho]/[2(1-2N rho)]. (C)

For q>=16, every positive-polynomial numerator term divided by 2^q decreases: N has degree two and N(q+2q^2) has degree at most four, with nonnegative coefficients; its successive ratio is bounded by ((q+1)/q)^4/2<1. The denominator increases since N/2^q decreases. Thus (C) is maximized at q=16, where exact rational arithmetic yields

    (C)|_{q=16}=186791/13540,
    14-186791/13540=2769/13540>0.

The whole derivation uses only affine-plane incidence, valid over every finite field, and integer inequalities valid for all q>=16. No extrapolation from q=2 or 3 is used. This proves the stated uniform PI-J certificate on an unbounded family. Small q data below serve as checks of the actual forest generator only; those small cubes are not in this sparse asymptotic regime.

### 6. Reusable linear-hypergraph certificate and exact universal gap

For any distinct positive width-w conjunctions on n covered variables with pairwise support intersection <=1, let N be gate count, k maximum read, rho=2^-w, uniform lambda=1/k, D=(1+rho/k)^N-1 and c=w+log D+log k>=log N>=0. Choose the same forest rule, using one gate whenever A lies in a support and otherwise a source-SCC forest. The entire preceding transfer argument gives

    R <=2{c[4N rho+4n k^2 rho^2]+2gamma Nw rho
             +4gamma n k^2 log w rho^2}
        +8N^2 rho^2{2[c+gamma w log w]
             +n[w+log k+2gamma log w]+max(0,log D)}.      (T)

This is a scalar, verifiable upper certificate, not an assertion that it is O(I) for every linear hypergraph. The extra max(0,log D) retains the possibility of a positive normalizer on generic dense inputs, while the affine certificate had log D<0. Width w=1 has log w=0; distinct singleton gates introduce no ambiguous duplicate columns. A clean-event lower bound I>=2Nw rho(1-2N rho) applies when 2N rho<1; otherwise this particular proof gives no useful influence lower bound.

The precise unpaid universal line is controlling the error-cost budget in (T) by I in arbitrary density and overlap regimes. When N2^-w is not small, the Boolean union can differ substantially from the sum of indicators; our crude E2 times worst-case forest cost may dominate I. Nothing here proves that every Boolean function has a prime-implicant table with small perturbation error. B03/A014 can consume (T) as a full-label/subset/root interface for their linear-hypergraph work. Broad arbitrary-density linear-hypergraph PI-J, overlapping intersections beyond one point, and universal FEI remain open.

## complete derivation or exact first unsupported line

For a fixed table define T=product_l(1+lambda_l*pi_l)-1=2^Lambda Z. For every nonempty spectral set A let W_A=sum_r 2^-B_lambda(A;r), summing distinct actual permitted partition-forest runs. Finite log-sum optimization gives inf_P(E_P B-H(P))=-log2 W_A, with minimizing posterior proportional to 2^-B. Consequently the complete optimized residual for this table is

R=sum_{A nonempty} fhat(A)^2 log2(T/W_A).

The factor T retains both activation normalization and nonempty-root conditioning. It is rational for conjunction gates. In particular it is not a sum of separately optimized root terms.

For assignment tau of each j in A to an incident gate, put B_l={j:tau(j)=l}, s_l=|B_l|, kappa_l=|A intersect R_l|, and list R_l in increasing physical coordinate order. Let a_{lj}=|A intersect strict predecessors of j|+1 and r_{lj} its rank. With M_l=1 and gamma=6/5, the run weight is exactly

2^-B = (product_used lambda_l)(product_roots 2^-|R_l|) D_tau^(6/5),

where D_tau=product_used(s_l/kappa_l)^s_l times product_assigned(a_{lj}/r_{lj}). This establishes the rational fifth-root interface used by the code.

Primary enumeration: construct the assignment graph l->k iff B_l intersects R_k. Enumerate every parent map with roots exactly one vertex per source SCC and no directed cycle. Enumerate every connecting coordinate for each edge. If a parent has c_j children attached through coordinate j, the queue has exactly product_j c_j! distinct child-label sequences: occurrences of distinct connecting coordinates have deterministic order; distinct child labels at an equal coordinate can be permuted. Sum this multiplicity. Assignments, parent maps, attachments and these sequences recover a unique actual queue trace; conversely each allowed partition trace recovers these data. Root order is fixed and unused gates are never visited. Thus no interchangeability entropy is omitted or counted twice.

NPN transport: input flips preserve Fourier squares and support incidence. An input permutation transports each ordered support along with the truth table. Hence a representative's table supplies an admissible table for every member of its orbit. Lexicographic gate orders on separate truth tables need not themselves be permutation invariant. Output complementation is evaluated explicitly and leaves H,I unchanged. The recorded chosen orientation supplies an existence upper bound, even when two orientation intervals overlap.

Exact certificates: Walsh coefficients are integers divided by 2^n; Parseval and a separate directed cube-edge influence count are asserted for every evaluated orientation. Prime conjunctions are identified by truth-cell containment and verified to union to the exact positive set. D^(6/5) is enclosed between adjacent 72-bit dyadics using integer fifth-power comparisons. For log x, scale to 1<=y<2 and use ln y=2 sum_{j>=0} z^(2j+1)/(2j+1), z=(y-1)/(y+1)<=1/3. After forty terms, the omitted tail is at most 2 z^81/[81(1-z^2)]. All intermediate nonnegative quantities are rounded outward to 80-bit dyadics; logarithm endpoints are rounded outward to 64 bits. Negative exponents and signed interval division use correctly ordered bounds and all four quotient corners. Rational inequalities comparing resulting endpoints are certificates, while floating midpoint sorting is only a convenience.

Weight-boundary handoff (analytic, for any finite fixed admissible support/order table): W_A(lambda) is a polynomial with nonnegative coefficients (algebraic for the rational prime-conjunction tables here), multilinear in the gate weights, since each gate is visited at most once. T(lambda)=product_l(1+lambda_l*pi_l)-1 is also multilinear with positive coefficients. Fix a positive packing vector mu and let lambda=t mu, 0<t<=1. Let d_A be the minimum number of gate supports needed to cover A. Any such minimum cover can be assigned nonempty pieces (otherwise it was redundant), and its assignment graph has a permitted source-root spanning forest. Conversely every run's used supports cover A. Therefore W_A(t mu)=c_A t^d_A(1+O(t)) with c_A>0. Also T(t mu)=t sum_l mu_l*pi_l+O(t^2). For the fixed finite Fourier law, exact logarithmic expansion gives

R(t mu)=D log2(1/t)+O(1), where D=sum_{A nonempty} P_f(A)(d_A-1)>=0.

The O(1) depends on the fixed table and direction; no uniformity over changing directions or dimensions is asserted. Thus uniform scaling to the all-zero boundary cannot lower the infimum when some positive-mass A requires two supports: it forces R to +infinity. If D=0, the ray has a finite limit determined by the leading coefficients, not necessarily divergence. This does not exclude a partial-weight boundary, or approaches whose direction changes with t. In particular one must still certify those faces when claiming failure of an infimum. The actual two-literal OR has d_{singleton}=1, d_{pair}=2 and pair Fourier mass 1/4, so D=1/4; its exact formula below independently confirms that coefficient. This finite-polynomial observation is a narrow optimizer handoff, not a new broad FEI candidate.

The complete bounded-class infimum is closed analytically for n<=2, allowing BOTH output orientations, EVERY positive admissible weight and EVERY full-support single-cover order for each prime conjunction. NPN leaves four types: constant, dictator, point defect and two-bit parity. A dictator has R=0 by single-root cancellation. A point's minority table has one width-two conjunction; lambda cancels, and the four Fourier squares are 1/4. Only the later singleton has rank charge 6/5, so R=3/10 and I=1, regardless of the two possible orders. The other output orientation has two disjoint literal primes with independent weights a,b in (0,1]. Put u=a+b, v=ab and T=u/2+v/4. Direct singleton/two-root masses give R=(3/4)log2 T-(1/2)log2 v+1. For fixed v, u>=2 sqrt(v) makes R smallest at a=b=t=sqrt(v). Then R=1-(1/4)log2 t+(3/4)log2(1+t/4), strictly decreasing on 0<t<=1 (derivative sign proportional to -1+ t/2). Its minimum is 1+(3/4)log2(5/4)>1>3/10. Thus choosing the minority table is the TRUE infimum for this bounded class, not merely a uniform-weight upper bound.

For two-bit parity both prime gates have the full support and pi=1/4. The only spectral set is A={1,2}. For arbitrary a,b>0 with a+b<=1, T=u/4+v/16 and W=u/4+v*2^(-12/5). Hence R=log2[(1+v/(4u))/(1+4*2^(-12/5)*v/u)]. Since 4*2^(-12/5)=2^(-2/5)>1/4, this decreases in v/u. The exact inequality v/u<=u/4<=1/4 gives the global minimum at a=b=1/2, for either output orientation and all gate orders. The exact ratio is (1/2)log2[(17/16)/(1+2^(-12/5))], about -0.081424729644. All boundary limits are included by these monotonic bounds. Constants are handled with R=I=0. Therefore the maximum TRUE bounded-class PI-J infimum divided by I on n<=2 is exactly 3/10. This closes continuous weights and all orders only in the declared all-prime, one-full-order-per-gate class; other representations are outside this claim.

The first unsupported universal line is R_PI-J(f)<=K I(f) for all dimensions with an absolute K, after optimizing one global lambda and the permitted order table. Nothing in the n=3,4 enumeration supplies that line or a lower bound on the lambda infimum there.

No extra gates, duplicate gates, multiple covers, partial support covers, or unrestricted nonpartition successful runs are in this menu. Each table's posterior is optimized exactly. Limiting zero-weight faces are included when analyzing the infimum, but actual admissible tables have positive weights. Constants are assigned R=I=0.

The exact finite result is

sup_{nonconstant f, n<=4} inf_{table in M(f)} R(f;table)/I(f) = alpha4 = (43+19 log2 3)/80 = 0.9139285939212746... .

Equality holds exactly on the 96 four-bit NPN images of OR(AND2,AND2). For every other four-bit function the optimal single-table ratio is at least 1/10 below alpha4, so its menu infimum is also strictly lower. This closes the worst-case variational constant of this declared bounded menu, NOT each function's individual prime-only infimum, arbitrary representations, or the all-dimensional conjecture.

**Single gate and local independent review of L1/L2.** For N=1, M=1 and any lambda>0, T=2^Lambda Z=lambda*pi, and every nonempty A has one partition forest with label-plus-root term log2(1/(lambda*pi)). It cancels log2 T. Thus lambda drops out exactly, including its limiting zero boundary. In a fixed full order, selected predecessor counts are 0,...,|A|-1, giving product_{j in A}(|A intersect predecessors(j)|+1)=|A|!. Therefore

R_S=(6/5)[sum_j Inf_j log2 r(j)-E log2 |A|!].

Swapping adjacent influences u<v at ranks r<r+1 changes the rank sum by (u-v)log2((r+1)/r)<0. Repeated swaps prove the optimum is decreasing influence order, with no floating optimization. For a general ordered M-cover, one root still cancels and the deterministic minimum-forest upper bound leaves I log2 M plus gamma/ln2 times the minimum rank cost; this reconstructs L1. This M-cover expression is a sufficient upper bound, not an identity for its entropy-optimized posterior. **Finite single-gate upper certificate.** On four bits only primes 2 and 3 occur in logs of ranks and factorials. If W_A are the integer Walsh coefficients, let J_j=sum_{A containing j} W_A^2 and L_s=sum_{|A|=s} W_A^2, with J_(1)>=...>=J_(4). Then

c2=6[J_(2)+2J_(4)-(L_2+L_3+3L_4)],

**Matching witness: positive prime side, ALL weights/orders.** The two positive primes are disjoint conjunctions, pi=1/4. Every spectral set has a unique assignment, and every used block is a root. Each block is used with probability 9/16. All four choices of within-block full orders have the same expected rank cost by within-block symmetry. For weights a,b in (0,1],

R(a,b)=(63/64)log2 T-(9/16)log2(ab)+27/10,

At fixed ab, a+b>=2 sqrt(ab), and T increases with a+b, so the minimum is at a=b=t. Differentiating the t-dependent part gives, up to a positive factor, -72+54t, strictly negative on 0<t<=1. **Matching witness: complementary prime side, ALL weights/orders.** The four complementary primes are the four choices of one falsified literal in each original block; their support graph is K2,2, each pi=1/4. with nonnegative rational c. Every gate is visited once, so no weight exponent exceeds one. T(lambda)=product_l(1+lambda_l/4)-1 is also multiaffine. Coefficients retain source-SCC root restrictions and distinct child sequences. prime_poly.py extracts them by assignment/parent maps; verify_continuum.py independently reconstructs all 300 set/table polynomials by actual queue growth and deduplicated traces, using a separate reachability/SCC implementation.

For a fixed positive-denominator coordinate box, W_A/T is a ratio of multiaffine polynomials. Holding other coordinates fixed makes it (a x+b)/(c x+d), whose derivative has constant sign. Repeated endpoint replacement shows its maximum occurs at a box vertex. The only zero-denominator vertex is the all-zero vector. The possible limiting values there are bounded by the largest one-gate leading coefficient divided by pi; if A requires two gates, this limiting mass is zero. The same bound follows along coordinate rays and positive mixtures of them. Hence every box, including boxes meeting origin and partial-zero faces, has a rigorous vertex upper bound m_A on W_A/T. # A011 / B03: representation existence

## exact target, quantifiers, hypotheses and units

For every finite selector decision tree on an independent uniform selector
cube, querying each selector coordinate at most once along each path,
and every collection of Boolean leaves on a common uniform data cube,
construct a gate cover and a complete whole-spectrum witness. Shared
variables, repeated leaf functions and colliding Fourier supports are
allowed. Entropy and code lengths are in bits; influence is the usual
uniform physical edge-flip probability summed over coordinates.

Let d_ell be leaf depth, p_ell=2^-d_ell, and D=sum p_ell d_ell. If each leaf
has a complete spectral witness code with expected length c_ell, the
constructed full code has expected length exactly

    2D + sum p_ell c_ell.

If I_sel(F)>=gamma D and c_ell<=K I(g_ell), its cost is at most
max(2/gamma,K) I(F). This is a genuinely explicit admission condition.
For unsigned nonempty character leaves, c_ell=0. Defining B as the expected
number of selector flips changing the character label gives I_sel=B/2.
The named class B>=beta D has a fully paid cost <=(4/beta) I(F).

For singleton characters the positive event is a union of ordinary
conjunction gates. The alternating two-label comb has beta=1/2,
unbounded worst-case read, repeated data labels, and I_sel/a tending to
zero. Its complete cost is <=8 I_sel and hence <=8 I(F).

Artifact completion: COMPLETE_LOCAL. Restricted mathematical claims:
AUTHOR_PROVED_PENDING_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW. Full representation existence
for every Boolean function with an absolute paid constant: OPEN.
Full FEI: OPEN. Novelty and public-release status: NOT CLAIMED.

## complete derivation or exact first unsupported line

The complete standalone derivation is STRUCTURED_COVER.tex. Its critical
steps are reproduced here for reviewers.

At a selector node with actual Boolean children G,H and residual Fourier
coefficients u_T,v_T, set q_T=(u_T^2+v_T^2)/2 and
theta_T=(u_T-v_T)^2/(4q_T). Choose a fair physical child, then its recursive
spectral witness with decoded set T, then a Bernoulli spectral bit Z with
parameter theta_T. The decoded parent probabilities are exactly

    q_T(1-theta_T)=(u_T+v_T)^2/4,
    q_T theta_T=(u_T-v_T)^2/4.

Both are the actual squared parent Fourier coefficients. The Bernoulli
law is valid by (u-v)^2<=2(u^2+v^2). Zero-q packets are never sampled.
This recursive construction retains the signs and all coherent cross
terms. It does not replace the Boolean children by normalized real
mixture components or use a false entropy-subadditivity claim.

The physical leaf path has probability 2^-d. Encode that prefix (d bits),
the complete leaf witness prefix, then exactly d selector-frequency bits
along the known queried path. Its Kraft sum is

    sum_ell 2^-d_ell [sum_w 2^-L_leaf(w)] 2^d_ell 2^-d_ell <= 1.

It is prefix-free and uniquely decodes the witness: physical paths are
prefixes ending at leaves; each leaf dictionary is prefix-free; the final
block length is fixed by the decoded path. Output spectral coordinates
are recovered from the leaf set and final membership bits. The true law
need not have uniform spectral bits, and their entire cost is still paid
at one bit each. Conditional physical leaf witnesses retain the original
leaf law because all later spectral innovations sum to one.

Let W be this exact witness and S its decoded output. Then
H(S)<=H(W)<=E L(W)=2D+sum p c. Pushing Kraft masses through the decoder
gives a complete subprobability reference Q(S); for every sampled w,
-log2 Q(S(w))<=L(w). Thus the full cross-entropy is also paid. Multiple
witnesses decoding to the same S are summed, not discarded or counted
as distinct output states. Their posterior entropy is present in
H(S)=H(W)-H(W|S).

The explicit cover is C_ell AND [g_ell=1], where C_ell is the conjunction
of the path literals. For character leaves, parity is itself a Boolean
combination of coordinate regular gates; singleton characters give
ordinary conjunction gates immediately. Finite truth tables provide an
algorithm for all child coefficients and witness transitions. Neither
efficient construction nor a short encoding of the static function's
dictionary is claimed or required by the reference interface.

Conditioning on selectors gives I_data=sum p I(leaf). The admission
I_sel>=gamma D pays the selector transcript, and the leaf codes pay only
data influence; the budget is never reused. Distinct unsigned characters
disagree with probability 1/2, proving I_sel=B/2 for that specialization.
Coordinates not fixed by the reached leaf stay in the same cell under
a flip, so B<=D. The condition B>=beta D is exact, physical, and checkable.

For the alternating-label comb, query j is reached with probability
2^-(j-1), so D=2(1-2^-a). Its continuation disagreement probabilities obey
r_a=1 and r_j=1-r_(j+1)/2, giving 1/2<=r_j<=1 and
B=sum 2^-(j-1)r_j>=D/2. Thus I_sel=B/2<1 while a grows. The cover has a+1
gates, each using x1, and the two data literals repeat without bound.

First unsupported universal line: an arbitrary Boolean selector with
shared/colliding leaf spectra need not have any representation with
I_sel>=gamma D for an absolute positive gamma. This line is not used in
the restricted theorem. For example, the first-positive comb with every
stopping leaf y1 and only its terminal leaf y2 has
D=2(1-2^-a) but B=a*2^-(a-1), so B/D tends to zero. The code can be
wasteful on a perfectly valid easy FEI function. Optimizing that cost
universally is a remaining obligation, not an inferred no-go for FEI.

This is a new complete reference interface in this run, not a claimed
bound on the original queue's variational minimum. Distinct-character
affine selectors are included as calibration only. Repeated labels and
low average selector energy are the stated extension of those baseline
hypotheses. Literature novelty remains unverified.

    J=sum_j 2^-j r_j=(1/2)sum_j(j+1)v_j.

rarity expectation by 2J/(e ln 2). Thus CE<=C_*J. The binary correction

# A014 — interference congestion with a paid exceptional mass

## exact target, quantifiers, hypotheses and units

Run: `20261011T223346Z-account05-A014-overlap-beyond-worst-case-read`, B03, A014. Full FEI remains OPEN. This stage proves the general interference lemma requested in B03 lead notes v1, supplies a complete queue-cost criterion, checks PP2 and PP3 exactly, and proves an L2 repair paying the PP_q rank/rarity bill for every prime q. Independent review is pending. The complete unbounded-read calibration is addressing, an already established FEI class; no new complete class theorem or priority claim is made.

All cubes are uniform; outputs are +/-1; Fourier coefficients are probability-normalized; entropy and all displayed costs use bits. Let f be an OR of N nonconstant Boolean gates h_l, each a combination of at most M regular functions. Let R_l be its relevant support, p_l=P(h_l=1), pi_l=min(p_l,1/2), b_l=log2(1/pi_l), a=6/5, gamma=120/11. Remove false constant gates; a true constant gate makes f constant and immediate. Set p(A)=fhat(A)^2, v=Var(f), I=sum_A |A|p(A).

For j with alpha_j=Inf_j(f)>0, partition d_j f into disjoint signed {0,+/-1} pieces d_jl by the least gate containing j that is pivotal when f is pivotal. Set alpha_jl=||d_jl||_2^2 and alpha_j=sum_l alpha_jl. Omit zero pieces. Define

    nu_j(T)=dhat_j(T)^2/alpha_j,
    rho_j(T)=sum_l dhat_jl(T)^2/alpha_j.

Both are probability laws. For A=T union {j}, let

    F_lj(A)=min_r ln[r_lr(j)/(|A intersect U_jlr|+1)],
    G_jl(A)=(a/ln 2) F_lj(A)+b_l 1[|A intersect R_l|<b_l/gamma],
    G_j(A)=min_{l:j in R_l} G_jl(A).

These are nonnegative. Let Gmax_j=max_T G_j(T union {j}). For any fixed kappa_j>=1 define the dimensionless exceptional mass

    epsilon_j(kappa_j)=sum_T (nu_j(T)-kappa_j rho_j(T))_+.

Zero denominators contribute zero: rho(T)=0 implies every piece amplitude and their sum vanish. No H(f) or assumed FEI inequality enters these definitions.

**Interference lemma.** For every such union and all choices kappa_j>=1,

    E_nu_j G_j <= E0+(24/5)log2 M+(24/5)log2 kappa_j
                  +epsilon_j(kappa_j) Gmax_j,                       (1)

where E0=(24/5)[log2(sqrt(2e)+2^(3/5))+log2 e]. The worst-event value is max_T nu_j(T)/rho_j(T), in which case epsilon_j=0. A smaller kappa is legal only with its explicit exceptional payment.

**Complete criterion.** Choose a global 0<lambda<=1 and the finite forest witness described below, using an assignment minimizing G_j. Write F(A) for the visited gates, s_l=|A_l|, ell_l=|A intersect R_l|. Let roots(A) be its roots and J_e the attaching coordinate of child edge e. Set

    Lambda_lambda=sum_l log2(1+lambda pi_l),
    S(A)=a sum_{l in F(A)} s_l log2(ell_l/s_l),
    L_lambda(A)=|roots(A)|log2(1/lambda)+sum_edges e log2 k_{J_e},

where k_i counts gates relevant to i. The following fully specified spectral congestion is sufficient:

    Gamma = [h2(v)+v Lambda_lambda+sum_{A!=empty}p(A)(S(A)+L_lambda(A))
              +(24/5)sum_j alpha_j log2 kappa_j
              +sum_j alpha_j epsilon_j(kappa_j)Gmax_j]/I.          (2)

For nonconstant f,

    H(f) <= [K0+E0+(29/5)log2 M+Gamma] I(f),                     (3)
    K0=120/11+3+2log2 3+log2(6e).

In particular the conservative bound K0+E0<218/5 is sufficient. This replaces all three worst-read costs by actual normalized root/label, subset, and interference bills. It does not assert a bound on Gamma for arbitrary unions. Gate/root names, normalization, and rarity are retained.

## complete derivation or exact first unsupported line

### 1. Proof of the interference lemma

For a piece d_jl, Section 5.4 gives the rank tail

    nu_jl(F_lj>t) <= M sqrt(2e) exp(-t/2),

and Lemma 5.3 gives

    nu_jl(ell_l<b_l/gamma) <= 2^(3/5) 2^(-5b_l/12).

If G_j>u then G_jl>u. Splitting its two nonnegative summands at u/2, with a=6/5, yields

    nu_jl(G_j>u) <= M (sqrt(2e)+2^(3/5)) 2^(-5u/24).             (4)

For the rarity event to contribute, b_l>u/2, so its probability has precisely the same exponent as the rank term. Weighted averaging with weights alpha_jl/alpha_j gives (4) for rho_j, with no read factor. These weights sum to one because physical supports are disjoint. Piecewise orthogonality alone without the source tail hypotheses would not establish (4).

Let delta_j(T)=(nu_j(T)-kappa_j rho_j(T))_+. Then for every E,

    nu_j(E) <= kappa_j rho_j(E)+delta_j(E).

Layer-cake integration over 0<=u<=Gmax_j gives

    E_nu_j G_j <= integral_0^infty min{1,kappa_j M A0 2^(-beta u)}du
                  +sum_T delta_j(T)G_j(T),

where A0=sqrt(2e)+2^(3/5), beta=5/24. To justify the minimum, nu(E)<=1 and nu(E)<=kappa rho(E)+delta(E) imply nu(E)<=min(1,kappa rho(E))+delta(E). The integral equals beta^(-1)[log2(kappa M A0)+log2 e], since kappa M A0>=1. Bound the last sum by epsilon_j Gmax_j. This proves (1). The sharper sum delta_j(T)G_j(T) can replace epsilon_j Gmax_j throughout.

A spectral-block sufficient condition is also useful. Suppose the fine pieces can be partitioned into groups of at most b pieces, and the sums D_B=sum_{l in B} d_jl have pairwise disjoint Fourier supports. At each T at most one grouped sum is nonzero, so

    dhat_j(T)^2=|Dhat_B(T)|^2 <= b sum_{l in B} dhat_jl(T)^2
                                          <= b sum_l dhat_jl(T)^2.

Thus kappa_j=b, epsilon_j=0 is valid. Fine-piece spectra need not be disjoint; cancellation inside a group is allowed. This criterion is different from merely assuming orthogonality in L2.

### 2. Proof of the complete queue criterion

Use the manuscript queue law, replacing the global root odds pi_l/k by lambda pi_l; retain subset selection, sizes, child counts and multisets. At attaching coordinate i choose uniformly among its k_i gates. The law remains a subprobability, since only successful finite runs contribute.

For each nonzero A, choose tau(j) minimizing G_jl(A), allowing a fixed deterministic tie rule depending on A; A_l={j:tau(j)=l}. Choose the manuscript directed spanning forest. Source components furnish roots. Distinct root supports intersect A in disjoint subsets, by the source-component argument in Section 5.3. The prescribed queue run visits each gate exactly once and outputs A.

Its root bill is Lambda_lambda+sum_roots[b_r+log2(1/lambda)]. Dense-root b_r's sum to at most gamma |A|, because b_r<=gamma ell_r and root intersections are disjoint. Each nondense root owns a variable, and its b_r is paid from the selected variable's G_j. All subset rank terms plus these sparse-root bills are therefore bounded by sum_{j in A}G_j(A), plus the dense-root charge gamma|A|.

The elementary symmetric normalizer obeys Z_s^l<=(6eM)^s. For an assigned variable i, its predecessor count plus one is <=ell_l, whence the subset weight bill is bounded by

    (a/ln2) F_li(A)+a log2(ell_l/s_l).

Summing gives |A|log2(6eM)+the rank bills+S(A). Size choices cost at most |A|log2 3. Child-count choices cost at most |A|(1+log2 3), since |F|<=|A| and sum c_l=|F|-|roots|<=|A|. Multisets cost at most 2|A|. Child gate choices cost exactly the child portion of L_lambda. Thus the probability of this one successful run supplies

    log2(1/Q1(A)) <= Lambda_lambda+(K0+log2 M)|A|
                     +S(A)+L_lambda(A)+sum_{j in A}G_j(A).       (5)

Set Q(empty)=1-v and Q(A)=v Q1(A) for A nonempty. Gibbs' inequality, with the empty atom handled exactly, gives

    H(f)<=h2(v)+sum_{A!=empty}p(A)log2(1/Q1(A)).

Also sum_{A:j in A}p(A)G_j(A)=alpha_j E_nu_j G_j by the derivative/Fourier identity. Average (5) and substitute (1). This proves (2)-(3), including v Lambda_lambda; no root normalizer has been dropped.

For a simple exact conservative constant, e<3, log2 e<3/2 (ln2>=2/3), log2 3<8/5 (3^5<2^8), and 6e<18<2^(9/2) give K0<22. Also A0<8 gives E0<(24/5)(3+3/2)=108/5. Hence K0+E0<218/5. We make no claim of sharp constants.

### 3. Explicit unbounded-read calibration with every charge bounded

For each integer a>=1 let m=2^a and

    f_a(x,y)=y_x,                 x in {0,1}^a, y in {-1,1}^m,
    h_u=1 iff (x=u and y_u=+1).

These m gates are regular oriented conjunctions, M=1, and their OR is f_a. Every selector belongs to m gates, so worst read k=m tends to infinity. Use the same desirability order in each conjunction: selectors in their common physical order, followed by its data coordinate. A Fourier set has exactly one data coordinate y_u and any selector subset T. For each selector j the rank expression is identical across all gates, while ell_u is one larger than ell_v for v!=u, so its rarity charge is no larger. Therefore assigning the entire A to u minimizes all G_j; choose u on ties. This gives a one-gate, one-root witness. Then S(A)=0 and L_1(A)=0 for every nonzero Fourier set. Note that the root's gate identity is paid through its independent root odds, not discarded.

Here pi_u=2^(-a-1), and

    Lambda_1=m log2(1+1/(2m)) <= (1/2)log2 e.

The function is balanced, v=1 and h2(v)=0. Its spectrum has exactly 2^(2a) coefficients of squared magnitude 2^(-2a), namely A=T union {y_u}. Thus H=2a, I=1+a/2; these identities are established controls, reproduced here rather than advertised as new class results.

For a data coordinate, there is one pivotal piece, so kappa=1. For a selector j, group the gates into neighboring address pairs u,v differing only at j. At a pivotal input exactly one of those two gates changes, and the two fine signed pieces are

    d_u = indicator(other address)*indicator(y_u=+1,y_v=-1),
    d_v = -indicator(other address)*indicator(y_u=-1,y_v=+1).

Up to the sign fixed by the j orientation their sum is

    D_{uv}=indicator(other address)*(y_u-y_v)/2.

Every nonzero Fourier index of D_{uv} contains exactly one of its two private data coordinates, hence different pairs have disjoint Fourier supports. The block criterion gives kappa_j=2, epsilon_j=0 for every selector, uniformly in a. Each selector has influence 1/2, so

    Gamma <= [(1/2)log2 e+(24/5)(a/2)]/(1+a/2)
           < 3/4+24/5.

Equation (3) gives H(f_a)<50 I(f_a) for all a. All label/root/subset/rank and normalizer costs are included. The original worst-read theorem gives 41+7a, which diverges; the new criterion is constant. The known exact H/I=4a/(a+2)<4 is stronger, and remains the preferred bound on addressing. The new information is the explicit bounded interference certificate within the complete queue criterion, not a new addressing theorem.

### 4. Exact PP tests and analytic obstruction to worst-event congestion

For prime q, use normalized nonzero triples over F_q as points and normal vectors; a line consists of triples orthogonal to its normal. There are n=q^2+q+1 points/lines, each line has q+1 points, each point lies on q+1 lines, and distinct lines meet once. PP_q is OR over all line conjunctions. Each line is a monotone minterm: on its own point-set assignment no other line is contained. Every monotone DNF representation therefore contains all lines, so the monotone-DNF minimum read is at least q+1. This assertion is deliberately limited to monotone conjunction covers.

Fix j. There are m=q+1 incident lines. Let A_l mean that all q other points of incident line l are positive; P(A_l)=2^(-q). These q-point sets are disjoint across the incident lines. Let B_r mean a nonincident line is all positive; there are q^2 such lines. The least-gate piece l is exactly A_l, none of the earlier A_t, and none of the B_r. For any t!=l,

    P(A_l intersect A_t)=2^(-2q).

Each nonincident line meets incident line l in one of its q other points, so its conjunction with A_l also has probability 2^(-2q). A union bound proves

    2^(-q)[1-(q^2+q)2^(-q)] <= alpha_jl <= 2^(-q).               (6)

The lower bound can be negative at small q; its asymptotic use is restricted to delta_q=(q^2+q)2^(-q)<1. All pieces are positive indicators. Hence their empty Fourier coefficients are alpha_jl and the sum's empty coefficient is alpha_j=sum_l alpha_jl. At this singleton Fourier event,

    nu_j(empty)/rho_j(empty)=alpha_j^2/sum_l alpha_jl^2
                    >= (q+1)(1-delta_q)^2 -> infinity.          (7)

Thus no uniform bound on the lead's worst-event kappa is possible for PP_q. This is an actual Boolean family refuting that congestion helper, not FEI. The equal-mass premise is false for the exact least-gate partition, but asymptotic equal masses make the obstruction stronger, not weaker.

Exact all-coordinate results:

| Family | I | least-gate masses for each coordinate (ordered) | max kappa |
|---|---|---|---|
| PP2 | 63/32 | 7/64, 3/32, 5/64 | 162/55 |
| PP3 | 5005/2048 | 107/2048, 199/4096, 185/4096, 43/1024 | 3698/925 |

PP2's maximum is realized at the empty residual Fourier index. PP3's empty ratio is 296450/74603, slightly below 3698/925: other events are also nearly maximally coherent. Exact epsilon(1), epsilon(2), rank expectation intervals and tail-event ratios are in `out/check.json`. For q=2,3 every nonempty incident intersection has ell>=1>b_l/gamma, so rarity is identically zero and the listed rank-only intervals are the full G statistic for the canonical sorted line order. This simplification is not extrapolated to large q.

### 5. L2 perturbation repair: PP rank term paid for every prime q

The failed zero-error helper admits a quantitative repair. The following general lemma does not require ideal pieces to have disjoint physical supports. Suppose ideal functions a_l have at most one nonzero Fourier coefficient at each index outside an exceptional index set E. For the actual disjoint physical pieces d_l put e_l=a_l-d_l, e=sum_l e_l, d=sum_l d_l and alpha=||d||_2^2. At T outside E, write a=sum_l a_l. Then

    dhat(T)^2 <= 2 ahat(T)^2+2 ehat(T)^2
              <= 4 sum_l dhat_l(T)^2
                   +4 sum_l ehat_l(T)^2+2 ehat(T)^2.              (8)

The second inequality follows because only one ideal amplitude is nonzero; for that index, |ahat_l|^2<=2|dhat_l|^2+2|ehat_l|^2. Consequently,

    epsilon(4) <= nu(E)+[4 sum_l ||e_l||_2^2+2||e||_2^2]/alpha.   (9)

Both the pointwise inequality and the L2 bill are explicit. No comparison of entropies of coherent and incoherent spectra is used.

For PP_q, let a_l=indicator(A_l) from section 4. Each a_l depends on its own q-point block; these blocks partition all points except j. Its Fourier coefficients vanish outside that block. Thus the ideal pieces have disjoint Fourier supports except E={empty}. The actual d_l is a subindicator of a_l. With m=q+1, D=q^2+q and delta=D2^(-q), the same union bound as (6) gives

    ||e_l||_2^2=P(A_l and not piece_l)<=D2^(-2q),
    sum_l ||e_l||_2^2<=mD2^(-2q),
    ||e||_2^2<=m sum_l ||e_l||_2^2<=m^2 D2^(-2q).

The middle pointwise Cauchy-Schwarz inequality holds even though the error supports overlap. Since nu(empty)=alpha, (9) and (6) yield, whenever delta<1,

    epsilon_j(4) <= alpha_j+(4+2m)D2^(-q)/(1-delta).             (10)

All rank orders have ranks at most q+1 and rarity charges at most b_l=q+1, so

    Gmax_j <= q+1+(6/5)log2(q+1).                               (11)

For every integer q>=16, delta<=1/2: at q=16 it is 272/65536, and q(q+1)2^(-q) decreases thereafter. Moreover m<=2q, D<=2q^2, 4+2m<=3q and alpha<=2q2^(-q). Equations (10)-(11) give

    epsilon_j(4)<=14q^3 2^(-q),
    epsilon_j(4)Gmax_j <= (308/5)q^4 2^(-q)<=308/5.              (12)

The last inequality is exact: 16^4/2^16=1 and the successive ratio ((q+1)/q)^4/2<1 for q>=16, since 17^4<2*16^4. For q<16, epsilon_j(4)<=1 and (11) gives Gmax_j<=104/5, so the same bound 308/5 holds. The small-q argument does not use a positive lower bound in (6).

Thus, for every prime q, every coordinate admits the **fixed choice kappa_j=4** and the all-dimensional paid bill

    sum_j alpha_j epsilon_j(4)Gmax_j <= (308/5)I(PP_q).

Substituting in (1), with M=1, gives

    sum_j alpha_j E_nu_j G_j <= [E0+356/5]I(PP_q) < 93 I(PP_q). (13)

The constant is conservative; (12) decays exponentially for large q. This proves a rank/rarity congestion replacement with unbounded actual read q+1 and bounded exceptional bill, even though zero-error worst-event congestion diverges. It uses spectral concentration of the **error of private-block ideal pieces**, not concentration of the masses of the actual pieces. The lead's equal-mass issue is therefore bypassed.

**First unsupported line for the complete PP_q theorem:** one fixed reference and its minimizing assignment have h2(v)+v Lambda_lambda+E[S+L_lambda]=O(I(PP_q)), with a uniform constant. Equation (13) pays the remaining rank term outright. The lead owns those root/label/subset estimates; they are not consumed as proved facts here. In particular, (13) alone is not a complete PP FEI theorem and does not close the universal conjecture.

## complete derivation or exact first unsupported line

The full source-complete proof is saved immediately in [DERIVATION.md](DERIVATION.md), hash-bound in CLAIMS/receipts. Its dependency chain is:

1. For any Fourier decomposition d=sum_l u_l+r, projected Young's inequality retains the exact signed cross sum:

       ||P_E d||^2 <=(1+eta)[sum_l||P_Eu_l||^2+sum_{l!=m}<P_Eu_l,P_Eu_m>]
                        +(1+1/eta)||P_Er||^2.

   The same holds for a nonnegative Fourier-cost multiplier. No cross term is discarded for an arbitrary union.

2. For positive AND gates at coordinate j, let S_j count satisfied incident residual clauses and B_j the event of a satisfied nonincident clause. Then d_jf=1[S_j>0]1[not B_j]. Writing a_j=sum_incident 2p_l, pairwise intersection estimates yield

       C_j=E[S_j(S_j-1)]<=2^(t-1)a_j^2,
       E[S_j 1[B_j]]<=2^t a_j(mu-a_j/2),
       ||d_jf-S_j||^2<=theta a_j,
       Inf_j(f)>=(1-theta)a_j.

   Thus Q=sum_j a_j=2sum_l w_l p_l and I>=(1-theta)Q. The ideal cross spectrum is nonnegative and has exact total mass C_j. Nonnegative products, rather than nonnegative individual FWHT amplitudes in every bit convention, are the required property.

3. A good Fourier set A is contained in some gate. Assign it wholly to the gate minimizing SUM_j G_jl(A). Its ideal diagonal weights (2p_l)^2 are identical across j in A, so the minimizing owner's total cost is at most the weighted average over owners. For a bad set all ideal derivative amplitudes vanish. With Gmax<=(11/5)W, the published piece tails and multiplier lemma give

       R<=[2E0+(44/5)theta W]Q,
       E_p[|A|1[bad]]<=theta Q.

   This averaged whole-set argument is not a claim that one owner minimizes each coordinate separately.

4. Use one fixed queue with root odds p_l and child-gate prior p_l/sum_incident p_m. Root normalization is Lambda=sum_l log2(1+p_l)<=mu log2 e. A child name costs <=w_l<=W, because mu<1. Good sets need one root and no child/subset congestion. Bad sets cost <=(11/5)W|A| in additional names and subset allocation, using log2 N<=W. Dense root rarity and sparse root rarity are paid in the original forest manner; all elementary costs contribute K0 I. Consequently

       H<=h2(v)+v Lambda+K0 I+L+S+R,
       L+S<=(11/5)theta W Q.

   Gibbs uses Q(empty)=1-v and Q(A)=v Q1(A). The term is v Lambda, not Lambda erased or an independently optimized normalizer.

5. Use h2(v)<=2I, v<=4mu, Q>=2mu, K0<22, E0<108/5. The exact final expression is

       H/I <24+[2E0+11theta W+3mu]/(1-theta)
            <24+[216/5+11/16+3/32]*(16/15)
            =10637/150<71.

6. The raw approximation has an exact dense read-one obstruction: on m disjoint width-w clauses,

       ||d_jf-u_j||^2/Inf_j=(1-2^(-w))^(-(m-1))-1 -> infinity.

   These functions already satisfy C003 with k=1. This refutes a density-free normalized raw-remainder helper, not FEI. Factor distant false-clause constraints into C_j. Its independence from the incident residual variables and decreasing/increasing covariance induction pay only nearby blockers. The exact local pressure theta_j in DERIVATION yields

       E_nu_j G_j <=[2E0+4theta_j Gmax_j]/(1-theta_j),
       R<(140/3)I<47I if all theta_j W_j<=1/16.

# A015 / B03: minterm label barrier, with activation normalization

## exact target, quantifiers, hypotheses and units

For every indicated finite Boolean family, quantify the charged label component in the Section 5 queue witness at the **fixed scale lambda=1/k**:

`C_lab(f,D) = sum_{A != empty} fhat(A)^2 min_tau |F_tau(A)| log2 k`.

Here D is a specified DNF, R_l is the physical support of term l, tau assigns every j in A to one term containing j, and F_tau is the set of used terms. Every such assignment has the source-component spanning forest required by Proposition 5.5. Define separately the allocation pressure `P_sub(A,tau)=sum_l s_l log2(|A intersect R_l|/s_l)`, whose coefficient in the proof is 6/5. Empty sets cost zero. All expectations below are **unconditioned** squared-Fourier expectations, and all logarithms are in bits. Conditional expectations given nonempty A must be multiplied by v=Var(f).

Two DNF conventions must be distinguished. FULL CELLS means one full-width signed conjunction for every input in the true event. PRIME means the canonical minimal positive conjunctions for the monotone examples. Calling both 'minterms' hides the tribes contrast.

Main outcome: fixed-scale labels already obstruct a dimension-independent payment for majority, even after optimal whole-set gate assignment. Prime tribes has zero label charge. Sparse activation does not make the majority barrier disappear. These are coding-component obstructions, not FEI counterexamples or lower bounds on every optimized reference. One bundled scoped diagnostic is submitted for review; no new universal representation lemma is asserted.

## complete derivation or exact first unsupported line

### 1. The fixed-scale component and why it is not a universal lower bound

At lambda=1/k, each forest root contributes log2 k as part of `log2(1/(lambda*pi_l))`; every child label is bounded above by log2 k. Thus the explicit refined bound charges exactly the formal component `|F| log2 k`, because roots plus edges equals |F|. The actual child contribution is log2 d(j_e), which can be smaller. This report minimizes the formal component over complete assignments. It does not replace it by the weaker coordinatewise `|A| log2 k`.

The complete law also has `h2(v)+v Lambda_lambda`, root rarity, subset normalizers/ranks, size choices, and attachments. It can sum probabilities of different successful witnesses. A lower bound on this **charged expression** is not a lower bound on `log2(1/Q(A))`, on entropy, or on all scales. Changing scale or erasing labels is permissible only in the full cost. The first unsupported line of any proposed universal conclusion would be: 'for every Boolean f there exists a complete normalized representation/reference whose expected total cost is <=K I(f)'. Nothing here proves it.

### 2. Majority: the label obstruction survives whole-set assignment

Let n=2a+1, t=a+1, a>=0; the true event is at least t positive bits. Its prime DNF has one term for each t-subset, each support of size t. The number of terms is N=binom(n,t), and the exact read is k=binom(n-1,t-1). These terms are mandatory in any exact DNF in the following sense: at the input whose positive set is exactly a given t-set, any satisfied implicant must require all t of those positive literals. Otherwise turn every unconstrained positive literal negative and obtain a false input satisfying that term. Distinct t-sets therefore require distinct terms. Each coordinate occurs in at least binom(n-1,t-1) terms in every DNF, even allowing negative literals or redundant terms. Such additions cannot make the formal fixed-scale label component less than log2 k because every nonempty spectral set needs at least one used term.

For the canonical prime DNF, the exact optimal count for a set A of size d is `ceil(d/t)`. The lower bound is support size. For the upper bound, partition A into groups of size at most t and extend each to a t-set; all extended groups are available terms. Since n<2t, this is one for d<=t and two for d>t. Thus, writing W_d=P(|S|=d) and T_n=sum_{d>t} W_d,

`E min |F| = 1+T_n`,

`C_lab(Maj_n,prime) = (1+T_n) log2 binom(n-1,t-1)`.

This is exact, not a bound using E|S|. Only odd levels have mass. A completely explicit spectrum is provided by

`b_d = 2^(-n) sum_{j=0}^n sign(j-t) sum_h (-1)^h binom(d,h) binom(n-d,j-h)`,

where sign(j-t) is +1 for j>=t and -1 otherwise (overall sign/input reversals do not affect W). Then `W_d=binom(n,d)b_d^2`. Equivalently, put `c_j=binom(2j,j)/4^j`; for d=2j+1,

`W_(2j+1) = [n/(2j+1)] c_a c_j c_(a-j)` (0<=j<=a).

One derivation of this last formula: for a chosen coordinate, the majority derivative is the indicator that the other 2a bits have exactly a positives. Its coefficient on 2j chosen bits is `(-1)^j c_a binom(a,j)/binom(2a,2j)`, obtained by taking the coefficient of x^a in `(1-x)^(2j)(1+x)^(2a-2j)` and dividing by 2^(2a). Squaring and multiplying by binom(n,2j+1), followed by factorial cancellation, gives the displayed W. The convolution identity `sum_j c_j c_(a-j)=1` then yields

`I(Maj_n)=n c_a = n binom(n-1,t-1)/2^(n-1)`.

Markov gives `T_n<=I/t=O(n^(-1/2))`. Wallis/Stirling gives `I~sqrt(2n/pi)` and `log2 k=n-1-(1/2)log2 n+O(1)`. Consequently

`C_lab/I ~ sqrt(pi*n/2) -> infinity`.

Actual entropy is exactly `H(W)+sum_d W_d log2 binom(n,d)`, and is Theta(sqrt(n)). The upper bound is baseline Theorem A, H<=C_reg I. For completeness a crude analytic lower bound avoids numerical extrapolation: c_l>=1/(2sqrt(l)) for l>=1 (square and induct using c_(l+1)/c_l=(2l+1)/(2l+2)). For a>=8 and integers ceil(a/4)<=j<=floor((a-1)/2), W_(2j+1)>=1/(8a^(3/2)); there are at least a/8 such j. Their degrees satisfy a/2<=d<=a and log2 binom(n,d)>=d>=a/2, since binom(n,d)>=(n/d)^d and n/d>=2. Therefore H>=sqrt(a)/128. The growing label/influence ratio is a code artifact while H/I stays bounded.

The allocation pressure is not the main obstruction. Among assignments using the minimum number of terms, its minimum is zero for every d<n. For d<=t use a term containing A. For t<d<n, split A into two parts with sizes each at least `d-t+1` and at most t, then fill both terms with coordinates outside A; their intersections with A are exactly their assigned parts. Such a split exists since d<=2t-2. For d=n every support intersection is t. Concavity of `s log2(t/s)` shows the minimum over partitions with s<=t is attained by sizes t,t-1: transferring size toward an endpoint cannot increase the sum. Thus

`E min P_sub = W_n (t-1) log2(t/(t-1)) <= W_n log2 e = O(1/n)`

(n=1 gives zero separately). The subsets giving minimum pressure also have minimum |F|. In contrast the generic bound is I log2 k. Neither allocation nor paying the same name once per whole set removes majority's remaining fixed-scale label bill. The generic (R) estimate still has `(24/5)I log2 k`; this report does not pay that term in this DNF.

The full-cell DNF has N=k=2^(n-1), all supports [n], and a one-gate assignment for every A. Its exact formal label charge is n-1; allocation pressure is zero. A direct n-bit characteristic-vector subset code would add a dimension bill; a size-first uniform code has cost `log2(d(d+1))+log2 binom(n,d)`. Its expected binomial term is already the conditional entropy in the displayed symmetric entropy identity. Full-cell naming is therefore distinct from coding the output set.

### 3. Tribes: prime supports remove the label term

Let T_(w,s) be the OR of s disjoint width-w all-positive tribes, w,s>=1. Put z=2^(-w), q=1-(1-z)^s and choose Boolean sign g=1-2T. Its canonical prime DNF has s disjoint supports and k=1. For a spectral set A, write J(A) for the number of hit tribes. Each hit tribe is mandatory and sufficient, so `min |F|=J(A)`; all gate-owned subsets have `|A intersect R_l|=s_l`. Therefore

`C_lab=0`, `P_sub=0`,

`E J=4s z(1-z)^s`, `I(g)=2sw z(1-z)^(s-1)`.

To verify the expectation, write `g=2 product_l (1-A_l)-1`. Every nonempty coefficient on a set hitting j tribes equals `2(-z)^j(1-z)^(s-j)` up to oriented signs, with multiplicity `binom(s,j)(2^w-1)^j`. Summing its squared mass gives v=4q(1-q); summing hit counts gives E J. The empty coefficient is 1-2q. This proves the normalization and count formulas directly.

The exact entropy is

`H = (1-2q)^2 log2(1/(1-2q)^2) - 2v + 2w E J + 2 log2(1/(1-z)) (s v-E J)`

with 0 log(1/0)=0. In the standard regime w->infinity, sz->lambda in (0,infinity), I~2lambda exp(-lambda)w and H/I->4 (A076 baseline). No entropy asymptotic is needed for the label obstruction.

The full-cell DNF instead has `N=k=2^(ws)-(2^w-1)^s=2^(ws)q` terms, all support [ws]. Consequently `E|F|=v`, `C_lab=v log2 N`, allocation pressure zero. In the same regime, `C_lab/I ~ 2(1-exp(-lambda))s/lambda -> infinity`. This large spurious charge disappears completely on passing to the prime DNF. A whole-set single-name code alone therefore suffices for neither representation: first the right structural supports must be chosen.

### 4. Arbitrary rare activated cores: exact mass, influence and dimension charge

Let g be any Boolean function on m declared data bits, q=P(g=-1)>0, and let A_r be a point indicator on r>=1 fresh controls, p=2^(-r). Define F=1+A_r(g-1). For data B!=empty and arbitrary control U, `Fhat(B,U)=p epsilon_U ghat(B)`. For empty data and U!=empty it is `-2pq epsilon_U`; the empty coefficient is 1-2pq. Thus

`v_F=4pq(1-pq)`, `I(F)=p(I(g)+2rq)`.

The nonempty-data sector has mass p Var(g), not p^2 Var(g): there are 2^r control sets. The control-only nonempty sector has mass `4p q^2(1-p)`. This is the normalization error to avoid when importing sparse-core intuition.

Full-cell terms for the activated event consist of its one fixed control point and one of the `N_-=2^m q` negative core assignments; every support is [r+m], so k=N_-, `min|F|=1` on nonempty A. Exactly

`C_lab(F,full cells)=4pq(1-pq) log2(2^m q)`,

`C_lab/I(F)=4q(1-pq) log2(2^m q)/(I(g)+2rq)`.

For balanced cores this becomes `(2-p)(m-1)/(I(g)+r)`. Allocation pressure is zero. Subset ranks, root rarity `(m+r)` per root, and normalization remain outside this label calculation.

For comparison with the actual target, if balanced,

`H(F)=p H(g)+2rp(2-p)+(1-p)^2 log2(1/(1-p)^2)`.

This is Proposition 8.9, independently checked coefficient by coefficient by the pilot. For general q the direct exact expression is

`H(F)=p H^+(g)+2rp Var(g)+4p q^2(1-p) log2(1/(4p^2 q^2))+(1-2pq)^2 log2(1/(1-2pq)^2)`.

No balanced approximation is used for the 810 arbitrary-core activation cases.

In particular take an m-bit odd majority core and r=ceil(2log2(m+1)). Then p->0, minority probability p/2->0, I(F)->0, but the full-cell charge/influence ratio is Theta(sqrt(m)). Its actual H/I stays bounded by the regular-gate theorem below. If r>>m the displayed label ratio vanishes; r cannot be silently omitted in classifying extreme regimes. Padding a fixed balanced core with dummy data bits increases this full-cell label charge linearly in padding while H(g) and I(g) remain unchanged; this makes the representation dependence unmistakable.

For the prime activated-majority DNF the supports are all r controls plus a t=(m+1)/2-subset of data. Every control occurs in N=binom(m,t) terms, and each data coordinate in binom(m-1,t-1); hence k=N. For a nonempty spectral set `(B,U)`, the exact minimum count is `max(1,ceil(|B|/t))`. Summing the two sectors gives

`E min|F|=2p-p^2+p T_m`,

`C_lab/I(F)=(2-p+T_m) log2 binom(m,t)/(I(Maj_m)+r)`.

Again this diverges as Theta(sqrt(m)) for the sparse choice r=ceil(2log2(m+1)). Assign all U controls to the first of the at most two used terms. Using the preceding majority data partition, pressure is zero for |B|<=t, at most r log2 e for t<|B|<m, and at most (r+1)log2 e at |B|=m. Thus `E P_sub<=p T_m(r+1)log2 e`. This is an upper bound for an explicit minimum-count assignment, not a claim of exact minimum activated pressure. The surviving label obstruction is not created by excessive subset congestion.

For completeness, activate tribes using their prime terms. If J(B)>0 the count is J(B), and if B=empty,U!=empty it is one. Controls have read s, data have read one, so k=s. Exactly

`E min|F|=4p q^2(1-p)+4p s z(1-z)^s`,

`C_lab/I(F)=[4q^2(1-p)+4s z(1-z)^s] log2 s/[2sw z(1-z)^(s-1)+2rq]`.

For sz->lambda, r->infinity and r=o(w), this ratio tends to `2[ (1-exp(-lambda))^2+lambda exp(-lambda)]/[lambda exp(-lambda)]`. More generally if r/w->rho>=0 and p->p_* it tends to `4[(1-exp(-lambda))^2(1-p_*)+lambda exp(-lambda)]/[2lambda exp(-lambda)+2rho(1-exp(-lambda))]`; log2(s)/w->1. Fixed r must retain p_*=2^(-r); rho>0 forces p_*=0. It stays bounded in these regimes, unlike the full-cell representation. Assign controls to one hit tribe. Other hit tribes contribute `b_l log2(1+|U|/b_l)<=|U| log2 e` each, giving `E P_sub<=p r log2(e) E_g J`. This explicit residual bound does not purport to pay all activated-tribes rank/normalization costs for arbitrary parameters.

### 5. Structural grouping repairs majority; a universal grouping lemma is still unpaid

Majority is a single regular gate. Activated majority is also regular: orient the event as increasing, put all controls before all data, and regard coordinates within each group as equivalent. If two inputs differ only by moving a 1 from data to a control, either another control is 0 and both outputs are false, or the input with this control 0 is false while the other is possibly true. Thus every control is at least as desirable as every data bit; data are exchangeable under the threshold. This is a proof of regularity, independently checked in the pilot. A one-gate representation has k=M=1, |F|=1, and zero (L) and allocation pressure. Theorem A pays the remaining complete entropy with C_reg<8.937. These are baseline gate-class consequences, not a new full-FEI case claim.

The precise missing feature in majority's fixed-scale DNF charge is **quotienting interchangeable minterms into a structural gate, or obtaining an equivalent posterior refund with all rarity/normalization bills retained**. The exact unpaid formal bill is `(1+T_n)log2 k`, already Theta(n), while its influence is Theta(sqrt(n)). Merely paying each label once per set improves I log k to this bill and still fails. Tribes shows that smaller physical supports can supply the needed grouping. Arbitrary cores do not come with a regularity order, cheap grouped gates, or a proved posterior refund.

An important algebraic sanity check: if N full-cell terms have the same support, same chosen rank order, and equal pi=2^(-d), the N distinct one-root/no-child runs selecting a fixed output subset have identical non-root factors. Their summed root mass is `N * 2^(-Lambda_lambda) lambda pi`. At lambda=1/N this cancels the explicit log2 N label charge exactly. The remaining factor is pi: the root rarity still costs d, in addition to Lambda and the subset factors. This is a valid finite multiplicity refund, not a universal proof or an assertion that optimal posterior cost must still be >=d. It explains why no raw-label barrier can be promoted to a lower bound on the complete optimized law. A fixed scale prior, root term, subset normalizers and posterior entropy must be assessed together as in C008 and the seed complete-reference lemma.
