The tracked quantity before this run was the sufficient local/tree criterion from the physical-refund report:

\[
L_{\mathcal T}\le K\sum_v\pi_v d_v+
{2\over3\ln2}V_{\mathcal T}+{1\over6\ln2}M_{\mathcal T}. \tag{0.1}
\]

Its status was **OPEN**, with an explicit request for a genuine sparse-suspension stress test. The new result below proves that even its one-node specialization is false for every finite `K`. More generally, every fixed linear price on `d,V,M` fails. The unpaid term is computed as

\[
d\log_2(1/\delta)+O(d),
\]

while `V=o(d)` and `M=o(d)`. This is movement from an untested sufficient candidate to an exact Boolean no-go theorem. It does not refute the possibility of a different stopping tree or a genuinely nonlocal charge.

## 1. Physical packet notation

For a coordinate split with Boolean children `G,H`, put, for every residual Fourier index `W`,

\[
a_W=\widehat G(W),\quad b_W=\widehat H(W),\quad
q_W={a_W^2+b_W^2\over2},\quad
e_W={(a_W-b_W)^2\over4},\quad
\theta_W={e_W\over q_W}.
\]

Zero packets are omitted. Then

\[
d=\Pr(G\ne H)=\sum_W e_W=\sum_Wq_W\theta_W,
\]

and the packet conditional entropy is

\[
L=\sum_Wq_Wh_2(\theta_W). \tag{1.1}
\]

The actual posterior-variance refund and the remaining-coordinate influence-variation refund are

\[
V=\sum_Wq_W(\theta_W-d)^2,\qquad
M=\sum_i(\operatorname{Inf}_i(G)-\operatorname{Inf}_i(H))^2. \tag{1.2}
\]

These are the one-node versions of the exact physical statistics in the pinned refund report.

## 2. Genuine Boolean sparse-activation family

Let `k>=4` be even, set

\[
r=2k,\qquad \delta=2^{-k},\qquad p=2^{-r}=2^{-2k},\qquad d=p\delta=2^{-3k}.
\]

On `k` data bits use the quadratic bent function

\[
b(x)=(-1)^{x_1x_2+x_3x_4+\cdots+x_{k-1}x_k}.
\]

Its Walsh coefficients `c_T` all have magnitude `\sqrt\delta`. Flip only the value at `x=0`:

\[
b'(x)=b(x)-2\mathbf1_{\{x=0\}}.
\]

On `r` control bits put `A(z)=\mathbf1_{\{z=0\}}` and define

\[
G(x,z)=1+A(z)(b(x)-1),\qquad
H(x,z)=1+A(z)(b'(x)-1).
\]

Finally let the physical selector coordinate `y` choose `G` or `H`. All functions here are genuine `{\pm1}`-valued Boolean functions. The two children differ only at `(x,z)=(0,0)`, so their selector disagreement is exactly `d=2^{-3k}`.

## 3. Packet formulas

For a data index `T` and a control index `U`, the coefficient difference is always

\[
\widehat G(T,U)-\widehat H(T,U)=2p\delta=2d,
\]

so

\[
e_{T,U}=d^2 \tag{3.1}
\]

for all `2^{3k}=1/d` packets, and their sum is `d` exactly.

If `T` is nonempty, the coefficient midpoint is

\[
m_{T,U}={\widehat G(T,U)+\widehat H(T,U)\over2}=p(c_T-\delta),
\]

therefore

\[
{q_{T,U}\over e_{T,U}}
=\left({c_T\over\delta}-1\right)^2+1
\ge {1\over4\delta}. \tag{3.2}
\]

The last inequality uses `|c_T|=\sqrt\delta` and `k>=4`. For empty data index and nonempty control index the midpoint is `p(\sqrt\delta-1-\delta)`; for the all-empty packet it is `1+p(\sqrt\delta-1-\delta)`. These formulas also show uniformly that

\[
\boxed{\max_W\theta_W\le4\delta.} \tag{3.3}
\]

## 4. The entropy retains the logarithm

For every packet, `q h_2(e/q)>=e\log_2(q/e)`. Sum only over the `(2^k-1)2^{2k}` packets with nonempty data index and apply (3.1)--(3.2):

\[
\begin{aligned}
L
&\ge (2^k-1)2^{2k}d^2\log_2{1\over4\delta}\\
&=(1-\delta)d(k-2). \tag{4.1}
\end{aligned}
\]

Thus `L/d` diverges linearly with `k`. In fact the explicit packet formulas and the expansion

\[
h_2(t)=t\bigl(\log_2(1/t)+\log_2 e+O(t)\bigr)
\]

give the sharper asymptotic

\[
\boxed{{L\over d}=k+\log_2e+o(1).} \tag{4.2}
\]

The empty-data packets contribute `o(d)`: their total mismatch mass is `\delta d`, and their posterior is `O(\delta^2)` except for the all-empty packet, whose contribution is smaller still. On nonempty-data packets `\theta_W=\delta(1+O(\sqrt\delta))`; their total mismatch mass is `(1-\delta)d`. This proves (4.2).

## 5. Both physical variance refunds lose the logarithm

Since `\sum q_W\theta_W=d`, (3.3) gives

\[
\begin{aligned}
V
&=\sum_Wq_W\theta_W^2-d^2\\
&\le (\max_W\theta_W)\sum_Wq_W\theta_W\\
&\le4\delta d. \tag{5.1}
\end{aligned}
\]

The influence variation is exact. `G` and `H` differ at one vertex of their `3k`-dimensional residual cube. Every neighbor of that vertex has common value `+1`; hence flipping the central value changes the pivotal status of exactly one undirected edge in every residual coordinate. Consequently

\[
\operatorname{Inf}_i(H)-\operatorname{Inf}_i(G)=2^{1-3k}=2d
\]

for all `3k` residual coordinates, and

\[
\boxed{M=3k(2d)^2=12kd^2.} \tag{5.2}
\]

In particular,

\[
{V\over d}\le4\delta\to0,
\qquad
{M\over d}=12kd\to0. \tag{5.3}
\]

The checker further confirms the exact asymptotics `V/d=\delta+o(\delta)` and (4.2); those refinements are not needed for the no-go.

## 6. Precise no-go theorem

### Theorem

For every finite constants `K,A,B>=0`, there exists an even `k>=4` and a genuine Boolean physical split from Section 2 such that

\[
\boxed{L>Kd+AV+BM.} \tag{6.1}
\]

Hence no dimension-independent one-node estimate of the form

\[
L\le Kd+AV+BM \tag{6.2}
\]

is valid for all Boolean functions. In particular, the one-node specialization of (0.1), with

\[
A={2\over3\ln2},\qquad B={1\over6\ln2},
\]

is false for every finite `K`.

### Proof

Divide by `d` and use (4.1), (5.1), and (5.2):

\[
{L-Kd-AV-BM\over d}
\ge(1-\delta)(k-2)-K-4A\delta-12Bk d.
\]

The right side tends to `+infinity` with even `k`. QED.

The theorem extends verbatim to any fixed finite collection of local posterior-moment credits `\sum q_W\Phi_j(\theta_W)` satisfying `\Phi_j(t)<=C_jt` near zero: each such credit is `O(d)`, while the entropy is `d\log_2(1/\delta)+O(d)`.

## 7. Exact scope and why FEI survives

This is a no-go for **local fixed-price variance/moment refunds**, not for the exact telescoping identities, not for every adaptive stopping tree, and not for FEI.

Indeed the residual child influences from the inherited construction are

\[
I(G)=p\,[k/2+r(1-\sqrt\delta)],
\]

\[
I(H)=p\,[k/2+2k\delta+r(1-\sqrt\delta+2\delta)].
\]

They are of order `kp`, while `L` is of order `kd=kp\delta`. Thus the full physical system has ample ordinary influence; the obstruction is that the proposed local refunds do not transport any of that downstream/child budget back to the rare selector packets. The unpaid logarithm must be amortized nonlocally, for example through a survival code, downstream child/leaf budget, or an exact logarithmic KL term. Charging only quadratic posterior fluctuation necessarily loses it.

The mandatory sparse-defect and rare-restriction falsifier is therefore decisive for (6.2). The construction is itself a sparse suspension of a bent source and hence also covers the near-tensor/sparse-activation failure mode. No universal replacement estimate is proposed here, so addressing/multiplexer and prime-gate checks are not claimed as evidence. They remain mandatory for any future positive all-gate statement.

The existing signed variational certificate recovers one half of the leading logarithm on the simpler one-point suspension, while the complete unweighted convolution `L^2` bank loses it. The present theorem adds that the exact physical variance refunds `V,M` also lose the logarithm, even though they telescope without reuse.

# B09 — product-biased restriction uncertainty: a prime-gate counterexample and an endpoint-safe repair

**Run:** `20261011T195500Z-account01-B09-biased-restriction-uncertainty`  
**Date:** 2026-10-11  
**Classification:** `PROVED_AUXILIARY_LEMMA_AND_REFUTED_HELPER`  
**Full uniform-cube FEI:** **OPEN / NOT PROVED.**

## 0. Result in one line

For a genuine Boolean gate under an arbitrary product measure, the physical-block entropy decrement still splits exactly as

\[
L_A=M_A+J_A,
\]

where `M_A` is the actual conditional spectral-label entropy and `J_A` is the physical-child mixture information.  The uniform estimate `J_A<=M_A` is **false** at nonuniform biases, already for the two-bit AND sign gate.  The following endpoint-safe replacement is universal:

\[
\boxed{
0\le J_A\le M_A+\Delta_A(p),\qquad
L_A\le2M_A+\Delta_A(p),
}
\tag{0.1}
\]

where

\[
\boxed{
\Delta_A(p)=\sum_{i\in A}
\left[h_2(p_i)+\log_2\max\{p_i,1-p_i\}\right].
}
\tag{0.2}
\]

At the uniform bias, `Delta_A=0`, recovering `J_A<=M_A`.  At a rare endpoint,

\[
h_2(p)+\log_2(1-p)
=p\log_2(1/p)+O(p^2),\qquad p\downarrow0,
\tag{0.3}
\]

so the repair retains the rare-event logarithm required by the current B05 obstruction.

## 2. Exact product-biased block ledger

Work on `{0,1}^n`.  Let the coordinates be independent with

\[
\Pr[X_i=1]=p_i\in(0,1),
\]

and use the orthonormal one-bit basis

\[
\phi_i(0)=-\sqrt{\frac{p_i}{1-p_i}},\qquad
\phi_i(1)=\sqrt{\frac{1-p_i}{p_i}}.
\]

For Boolean `f`, write `hat f_p(S)` for the resulting product-biased Fourier coefficients and

\[
\mu(S)=\widehat f_p(S)^2.
\]

Fix a block `A` and put `B=[n]\setminus A`.  For a physical assignment `z` on `A`, let `f_z` be the restricted Boolean function on `B`, with the inherited product biases, and let `mu_z` be its biased spectral law.  For `S~mu`, write `S_A=S cap A` and `S_B=S cap B`.  Define

\[
M_A:=H(S_A\mid S_B),
\]

\[
J_A:=H(S_B)-\mathbb E_{z\sim\mu_{p_A}}H(\mu_z),
\]

and

\[
L_A:=H(\mu)-\mathbb E_zH(\mu_z).
\]

Exactly as in the uniform physical-restriction identity,

\[
\boxed{L_A=M_A+J_A.}
\tag{2.1}
\]

Indeed, biased Parseval on the revealed coordinates gives

\[
q_T:=\Pr[S_B=T]
=\sum_{R\subseteq A}\widehat f_p(R\cup T)^2
=\mathbb E_z\widehat{f_z}_{p_B}(T)^2.
\]

Thus the average child law is exactly the parent marginal `q`, so entropy concavity gives `J_A>=0`, and the chain rule gives (2.1).  Equivalently, under the joint experiment `Z~mu_{p_A}`, then `T~mu_Z`,

\[
J_A=I(Z;T).
\tag{2.2}
\]

All signs, child normalizations, physical branch probabilities, and zero masses remain in this identity.

## 3. PROVED: biased uncertainty bound with explicit rare-event tax

### Theorem B09-BIASED-BLOCK-UNCERTAINTY-01

For every finite Boolean `f`, every interior product-bias vector `p`, and every physical block `A`, equations (0.1)--(0.2) hold.

### Proof

Fix `T subseteq B` with `q_T>0` and define the normalized spectral-fiber vector

\[
a_R=\frac{\widehat f_p(R\cup T)}{\sqrt{q_T}},
\qquad R\subseteq A.
\]

Its squared entries have entropy `H(S_A | S_B=T)`.  Define the normalized physical posterior vector

\[
b_z=\frac{\sqrt{\mu_{p_A}(z)}\,\widehat{f_z}_{p_B}(T)}{\sqrt{q_T}},
\qquad z\in\{0,1\}^A.
\]

Its squared entries are the conditional law `Pr[Z=z | T]`.

The two vectors are related by the tensor orthogonal matrix

\[
b=U_Aa,
\qquad
U_A=\bigotimes_{i\in A}
\begin{pmatrix}
\sqrt{1-p_i}&-\sqrt{p_i}\\
\sqrt{p_i}&\sqrt{1-p_i}
\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{3.1}
\]

The largest absolute matrix entry is

\[
c_A=\prod_{i\in A}\sqrt{\max\{p_i,1-p_i\}}.
\]

Maassen--Uffink therefore gives, fiber by fiber,

\[
H(a^2)+H(b^2)
\ge-2\log_2c_A
=-\sum_{i\in A}\log_2\max\{p_i,1-p_i\}.
\tag{3.2}
\]

Average (3.2) with weights `q_T`.  The first average is `M_A`; the second is `H(Z|T)`.  Since

\[
J_A=H(Z)-H(Z\mid T),
\qquad
H(Z)=\sum_{i\in A}h_2(p_i),
\]

we obtain

\[
J_A\le M_A+\Delta_A(p).
\]

Together with `L_A=M_A+J_A` and `J_A>=0`, this proves (0.1).  The endpoint expansion (0.3) follows by expanding `h_2(p)` and `log_2(1-p)`; the linear `p/ln 2` terms cancel.  QED.

### Scope

This is a product-biased restriction lemma.  It is not a strong FEI inequality for arbitrary weighted thresholds, and it does not bound `M_A` by influence.  Its value is to identify exactly how the uniform Walsh uncertainty payment degrades at biased gate inputs.

## 4. REFUTED: the tax-free biased extension

### Candidate B09-TAXFREE-BIASED-UNCERTAINTY (false)

> For every genuine Boolean gate, every interior product bias, and every physical block `A`, `J_A<=M_A`.

Take the essential two-input Boolean gate

\[
g(x,y)=(-1)^{xy},
\]

which is AND up to the sign/output convention.  Let

\[
p=\Pr[X=1]=\frac18,
\qquad
q=\Pr[Y=1]=\frac14,
\qquad A=\{X\}.
\]

The exact squared biased Fourier masses, in the order `empty,{X},{Y},{X,Y}`, are

\[
\boxed{
\left(\frac{225}{256},\frac7{256},\frac3{256},\frac{21}{256}\right).
}
\tag{4.1}
\]

The residual spectral bit has probability

\[
\Pr[S_Y=1]=\frac3{32}.
\]

The `X=0` child is constant, while the `X=1` child is the `Y` character, whose biased spectral nonempty mass is `3/4`.  Hence

\[
M_A
=H\left(\frac{225,7,3,21}{256}\right)-h_2\left(\frac3{32}\right),
\tag{4.2}
\]

\[
J_A
=h_2\left(\frac3{32}\right)-\frac18h_2\left(\frac34\right).
\tag{4.3}
\]

The rational atanh-series interval certificate gives

\[
0.227909707141212807<M_A<0.227909707141212808,
\]

\[
0.347454723165637765<J_A<0.347454723165637766,
\]

and therefore

\[
\boxed{
0.119545016024424957
<J_A-M_A<
0.119545016024424958.
}
\tag{4.4}
\]

Thus the tax-free extension fails by more than `0.1195` bits on the smallest nonlinear genuine Boolean gate.  This is a gate-helper counterexample, not an FEI counterexample: it says nothing about unbounded `H/I`.

## 5. Composition and prime-gate consequences

O'Donnell--Tan's product-biased composition theorem already reduces disjoint read-once compositions to gate inequalities at the induced output biases.  The exact matrix in (3.1) is compatible with that reduction: it is a tensor product on disjoint blocks, and both `Delta_A` and the aligned `M_A,J_A` ledgers add.

Therefore:

1. decomposable gates do not create a new violation of (0.1) beyond their factors;
2. the two-bit AND gate proves that a prime-gate proof cannot simply transplant the uniform `J<=M` statement to induced nonuniform biases;
3. a composition proof using this uncertainty route must either pay `Delta_A(p)` once, amortize it against a hierarchy credit, or exploit stronger Boolean phase constraints;
4. because `Delta(p)=p log_2(1/p)+O(p^2)`, replacing it by `O(p)` is impossible at the endpoint scale relevant to rare activation.

The unpaid universal implication remains a dimension-free payment of the actual conditional label cost `M_A` plus the nonreused endpoint tax by the appropriate biased influence/gate potential.

## 6. Required obstruction suite

### Addressing / multiplexers

Thus the uniform inequality is sharp and the whole address label is shared, rather than charged separately for each spectral coordinate.  Deterministic checks cover `m=1,2,3`.

### Sparse defects and rare restrictions

Full-block restrictions of one-point defects give the opposite endpoint `J_A=0`, `M_A=H`.  Checks cover dimensions `2..8`.  Trigger-block restrictions of majority-3 activated by `k=1..5` rare bits retain the full conditional cost and satisfy the proved inequality.  Analytically, (0.3) shows that the repaired theorem retains, rather than suppresses, the rare-event logarithm exposed by B05.

For exact disjoint products and aligned blocks, the spectral law, physical posterior channel, `M`, `J`, and `Delta` all tensorize additively.  The checker includes quadratic bent tensors through seven factors.  This theorem makes no continuity claim for coherent near-tensor surgery; such a claim would need to pay the known `alpha^2 log(1/alpha^2)` term.

## 1. Claim under review

For a physical split with Boolean children `G,H`, write

\[
q_W={\widehat G(W)^2+\widehat H(W)^2\over2},\qquad
e_W={\bigl(\widehat G(W)-\widehat H(W)\bigr)^2\over4},
\]

\[
\theta_W={e_W\over q_W},\qquad
d=\sum_We_W,
\]

\[
L=\sum_Wq_Wh_2(\theta_W),\quad
V=\sum_Wq_W(\theta_W-d)^2,quad
M=\sum_i(\operatorname{Inf}_i(G)-\operatorname{Inf}_i(H))^2.
\]

B05 claims:

> For every finite `K,A,B>=0`, some genuine Boolean physical split satisfies
> \[
> L>Kd+AV+BM.
> \]

The proposed witness uses even `k>=4`,

\[
\delta=2^{-k},\qquad p=2^{-2k},\qquad d=p\delta=2^{-3k},
\]

a `k`-bit quadratic bent function `b`, its one-point flip `b'`, and a `2k`-bit activation mask. This is a claim about a local fixed-price payment inequality, not FEI itself.

## 2. Independent analytic reconstruction

### 2.1 Boolean realizability and exact mismatch

The functions

\[
b(x)=(-1)^{x_1x_2+\cdots+x_{k-1}x_k},
\qquad b'(x)=b(x)-2\mathbf1_{\{x=0\}}
\]

are genuinely `{\pm1}`-valued because `b(0)=1`. With `A(z)=\mathbf1_{\{z=0\}}`,

\[
G=1+A(b-1),\qquad H=1+A(b'-1)
\]

are also Boolean. They differ at exactly one point of the residual `3k`-cube, hence

\[
d=2^{-3k}.
\]

This verifies the actual Boolean source; no arbitrary spectral law is substituted.

### 2.2 Fourier packet calculation

Every Walsh coefficient of the bent source has magnitude `sqrt(delta)`. The point flip subtracts `2 delta` from every data coefficient, while the activation mask contributes the factor `p` to every control coefficient. Consequently

\[
\widehat G(T,U)-\widehat H(T,U)=2p\delta=2d
\]

for all `2^{3k}` packets. Thus

\[
e_{T,U}=d^2,qquad \sum_{T,U}e_{T,U}=2^{3k}d^2=d.
\]

For nonempty data index `T`, the midpoint is `p(c_T-delta)`, so

\[
{q_{T,U}\over e_{T,U}}
=\left({c_T\over\delta}-1\right)^2+1.
\]

Put `x=delta^{-1/2}>=4`. For the smaller sign case this is `(x-1)^2+1`, and

\[
(x-1)^2+1\ge{x^2\over4}={1\over4\delta}.
\]

The negative sign is larger. For empty data index and nonempty control index, the corresponding ratio is `(x^2-x+1)^2+1`; the all-empty packet is larger still. Therefore

\[
\max_W\theta_W\le4\delta
\]

is valid for every even `k>=4`.

### 2.3 Entropy lower bound and asymptotic

Since `h_2(t)>=t log_2(1/t)`,

\[
q_Wh_2(\theta_W)\ge e_W\log_2(q_W/e_W).
\]

There are `(2^k-1)2^{2k}` nonempty-data packets. Hence

\[
L\ge(2^k-1)2^{2k}d^2(k-2)
=(1-\delta)d(k-2).
\]

For those packets,

\[
\theta_W={\delta\over1-2\sigma_W\sqrt\delta+2\delta}
=\delta(1+O(\sqrt\delta)),
\]

and their total mismatch mass is `(1-delta)d`. Empty-data packets carry only `delta d` mismatch mass. Applying

\[
h_2(t)=t\left(\log_2{1\over t}+\log_2e+O(t)\right)
\]

gives

\[
{L\over d}=k+\log_2e+o(1).
\]

The original asymptotic and lower bound are correct.

### 2.4 Refund sizes

Using `sum q_W theta_W=d`,

\[
V=\sum_Wq_W\theta_W^2-d^2
\le (\max_W\theta_W)d
\le4\delta d.
\]

For `M`, the two children differ at the central vertex only. Every one-bit neighbor has common value `+1`: for a data neighbor the quadratic exponent is zero, and for a control neighbor the activation mask is off. Thus one undirected edge changes pivotal status in each of the `3k` residual coordinates. Under the standard directed-edge influence convention,

\[
\operatorname{Inf}_i(H)-\operatorname{Inf}_i(G)=2^{1-3k}=2d,
\]

so

\[
M=3k(2d)^2=12kd^2.
\]

### 2.5 Quantifier check

For fixed finite `K,A,B>=0`,

\[
{L-Kd-AV-BM\over d}
\ge(1-\delta)(k-2)-K-4A\delta-12Bk d.
\]

Along even `k`, the right side tends to `+infinity`. The existential quantifier in the B05 theorem follows. No uniformity, endpoint, zero-packet, or sign case is missing.

## 3. Independent exact finite witness

The original checker compresses packets into four multiplicity classes. The review checker is independent in method: it constructs `G,H` from their full truth tables at `k=4`, performs an integer fast Walsh--Hadamard transform, and checks each of all 4,096 Fourier packets using `fractions.Fraction`. Only the entropy evaluation uses 80-digit `Decimal` arithmetic.

Exact reconstruction produced

\[
\sum_Wq_W=1,qquad
\sum_We_W={1\over4096},qquad
\max_W\theta_W={1\over10},
